children.translated_text: Chapter One
First Session
Salutation to the <s>Arhat</s>, whose nature is knowledge, power, and bliss,
<s>Anantadarśana</s> (Infinite Perception)
the ford of <s>dharma</s>, the Protector. (1)
who through compassion established
To cultivate the seed [of enlightenment] through the practice of reality by the wise,
<s>Bodhi</s> (Enlightenment):
this commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on our own Jain philosophical sūtras is composed. (2)

children.text: ननु यदि भवदीयानीमानि जैनसिद्धान्तसूत्राणि तर्हि भवतः पूर्वं कानि किमीया

children.translated_text: These sciences are beginningless; they are renewed

children.text: भ्योऽपि पूर्वं कानि किमीयानि वा व्याकरणादिसूत्राणीत्येतदपि पर्यनुयुङ्क्ष्व ! अनादय
children.translated_text: by the intention to present them in condensed or expanded form, and are attributed to their respective authors. Have you not heard the saying:

children.text: एवैता विद्याः संक्षेपविस्तरविवक्षया नवनवीभवन्ति तत्तत्कर्तृकाश्चोच्यन्ते । किं नाश्रौषीः
children.translated_text: 'The world was never otherwise than this'? Or consider the <s>Tattvārthasūtras</s> composed by <s>Vācakamukhya</s> [<s>Umāsvāti</s>],

children.text: न कदाचिदनीदृशं जगत् इति ? यदि वा प्रेक्षस्व वाचकमुख्यविरचितानि सकलशास्त्र
children.translated_text: which are the crest-jewel of all scriptures.

Objection: If these are your Jain philosophical sūtras, then what existed before you — were they yours or someone else's? You ask too little! Ask also whether the sūtras of grammar and the like belonged to anyone before <s>Pāṇini</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Akṣapāda</s>, and others!

children.text: यद्येवम्--अकलङ्क-धर्मकीर्त्त्यादिवत् प्रकरणमेव किं नारभ्यते, किमनया सूत्र

children.translated_text: What is this eagerness

children.text: रुषिकया ? मैवं वोचः; भिन्नरुचिर्ह्ययं जनः ततो नास्य स्वेच्छाप्रतिबन्धे
children.translated_text: for sūtra-making? Do not speak thus! For people have diverse tastes, and there is no worldly
or royal decree that restricts one's own choice — this is a trivial [objection].
If so — why not compose a <s>prakaraṇa</s> (treatise) like <s>Akalaṅka</s> or <s>Dharmakīrti</s>?

children.text: तत्र वर्णसमूहात्मकैः पदैः, पदसमूहात्मकैः सूत्रैः, सूत्रसमूहात्मकैः प्रकरणैः,

children.translated_text: with sessions (<s>āhnikas</s>) consisting of collections of sections, and with five chapters consisting of collections of sessions — the teacher composed this śāstra.
And for the purposeful engagement of the wise, to state the subject matter, this is the opening sūtra:
Therein, with words consisting of collections of letters, with sūtras consisting of collections of words, with sections (<s>prakaraṇas</s>) consisting of collections of sūtras,
Now, the investigation of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇamīmāṃsā</s>). (Sūtra 1)
through the exposition of the purport of all śāstras,
the wise are instructed and motivated [to proceed].

children.text: आनन्तर्यार्थो वा अथ-शब्दः, शब्द-काव्य-छन्दोनुशासनेभ्योऽनन्तरं प्रमाणं मीमांस्यत
children.translated_text: Or, the word '<s>atha</s>' means 'after' — meaning: after the sciences of grammar, poetics, and prosody, <s>pramāṇa</s> is now to be investigated.
By this, he states the single authorship [of this work] with the grammar-sciences and the like.
And the word '<s>atha</s>' in its topical sense,
like the sight of garlands, water-pots, and the like at a ceremony, serves also as an auspicious beginning. And

children.text: च सति परिपन्थिविघ्नविघातात् अक्षेपेण शास्त्रसिद्धिः, आयुष्म
children.translated_text: when there is an auspicious beginning, by the destruction of obstacles and adversaries, the accomplishment of the śāstra follows, and
the listeners attain long life.
The salutation to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> and the like,

children.text: कं तु मङ्गलं कृतमपि न निवेशितं लाघवार्थिना
children.translated_text: though already performed as an auspicious act, was not inserted [in the sūtra] by the sūtra-maker
for the sake of brevity.
'<s>Atha</s>' (Now) — since this word has the meaning of introducing a topic, by naming the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid knowledge) that is being treated by the śāstra,

children.text: दिव्यवच्छेदेन मीयते परिच्छिद्यते वस्तुतत्त्वं येन तत् प्रमाणं प्र
children.translated_text: determined with excellence, by removing doubt and the like — is <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid knowledge), the most effective instrument of <s>pramā</s> (true cognition).

children.text: मायां साधकतमम्, तस्य मीमांसा--उद्देशादिरूपेण पर्यालोचनम् । त्रयी हि शास्त्रस्य प्रवृ
children.translated_text: Its <s>mīmāṃsā</s> (investigation) consists of examination in the form of enumeration (<s>uddeśa</s>) and the like. For the procedure of the śāstra is threefold:

children.text: त्तिः--उद्देशो लक्षणं परीक्षा च । तत्र नामधेयमात्रकीर्त्तनमुद्देशः, यथा इदमेव सूत्रम् । उद्दिष्ट
children.translated_text: enumeration, definition, and examination. Therein, mere naming is enumeration — such as this very sūtra. The statement of the distinctive property of what has been enumerated

children.text: स्यासाधारणधर्म्मवचनं लक्षणम् । तद् द्वेधा सामान्यलक्षणं विशेषलक्षणं च । सामान्य
children.translated_text: is the definition. That is twofold: general definition and specific definition. The general
definition is the very next sūtra. The specific definition is:
'<s>Viśadaḥ pratyakṣam</s>' (The clear [cognition] is perception),
The division-
part,
however,
is itself a component of the specific definition

children.text: ङ्गमिति न पृथगुच्यते । लक्षितस्य इदमित्थं भवति नेत्थम् इति
children.translated_text: and hence is not stated separately. The examination of what has been defined — 'this is thus, not thus' —
through reasoning, is examination (<s>parīkṣā</s>), as in the third
sūtra.
That by which the reality of an object is measured — that is,

children.text: पूजितविचारवचनश्च मीमांसा-शब्दः । तेन न प्रमाणमात्रस्यैव विचारोऽत्राधि

children.translated_text: but also of the philosophical standpoints (<s>nayas</s>) which are aspects of it, purified through the refutation of erroneous views —
for these too [are part of the investigation].
<s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>nayas</s>, apprehension [of reality occurs]'
'By
(<s>Tattvārthasūtra</s> 1.6).
Thus says <s>Vācakamukhya</s>, [referring to] the means [of liberation] and the counterparts
of <s>mokṣa</s>
(liberation), crowned among all human goals.

children.text: क्षस्य मोक्षस्य च । एवं हि पूजितो विचारो भवति । प्रमाणमात्र
children.translated_text: Thus the investigation is revered. A mere investigation of <s>pramāṇa</s>

children.text: विचारस्तु प्रतिपक्षनिराकरणपर्यवसायी वाक्कलहमात्रं स्यात् । तद्विवक्षायां तु
children.translated_text: that culminates only in the refutation of the opponent's position would be mere verbal quarrel. If that were intended, then
the examination of <s>pramāṇa</s>'
'now,
(<s>Pramāṇaparīkṣā</s>, p. 1)

children.text: टिप्पणकारस्य भ्रान्तिः मूलादायाता भाति । वस्तुतः प्रमाणपरीक्षा न अकलङ्ककृता किन्तु विद्यानन्दकृता -

children.translated_text: this alone would have been [the title]. Therefore it is established: the teacher employed the word '<s>mīmāṃsā</s>'
in order to express the path of the objects-to-be-known purified by <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>naya</s>,

children.text: र्गं सोपायं सप्रतिपक्षं मोक्षं विवक्षितुं मीमांसाग्रहणमकार्याचार्येणेति ॥ १ ॥
children.translated_text: together with the means and the counterparts of <s>mokṣa</s>. (1)
And the word '<s>mīmāṃsā</s>' means 'revered investigation.' Therefore, not merely the investigation of <s>pramāṇa</s> alone is treated here,
Therein, he states the general definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>:
Correct ascertainment of an object is <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid knowledge). (Sūtra 2)

children.text: प्रमाणम्-इति लक्ष्यनिर्द्देशः, शेषं लक्षणम्, प्रसिद्धानुवादेन ह्यप्रसिद्धस्य विधानं
लक्षणार्थः । तत्र यत्तदविवादेन प्रमाणमिति धर्म्मि प्रसिद्धं तस्य सम्यगर्थनिर्णयात्मकत्वं
children.translated_text: Therein, the <s>dharmin</s> (substrate) which is well-known without dispute as '<s>pramāṇa</s>' — the property of its being the correct ascertainment of an object

children.text: धर्मो विधीयते । अत्र प्रमाणत्वादिति हेतुः । न च धर्म्मिणो हेतुत्वमनुपपन्नम्; भवति
children.translated_text: is prescribed. Here, 'because it is <s>pramāṇa</s>' is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). Nor is it improper for the <s>dharmin</s> to serve as the reason; for
the universal [nature] of the <s>dharmin</s> serves as the reason for the particular,

children.text: धर्म्मिणि तत्सामान्यं हेतुः, यथा अयं धूमः साग्निः, धूमत्वात्, पूर्वोपलब्ध
children.translated_text: as [in the inference]: 'This is smoke, it has fire, because it is smoke, like previously observed smoke.' Nor is it the case that without an example there is no probative force; for the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is established through internal pervasion alone, as in

children.text: धूमवत् । न च दृष्टान्तमन्तरेण न गमकत्वम्; अन्तर्व्याप्त्यैव साध्यसिद्धेः, सात्मकं
children.translated_text: 'A living body possesses a self, because it has breath and the like' — as will be shown.

'<s>Pramāṇa</s>' — this is the indication of the definiendum; the rest is the definition. For the purpose of a definition is to prescribe what is not well-known through the restatement of what is well-known.

children.text: प्रथमाक्षसन्निपातेन यत् ज्ञानम् । यद्यप्यनध्यवसाय एव निर्विकल्पकं तथाप्याहत्य सौगतमतनिराकरणा

children.translated_text: error
(indeterminate cognition). Therefore, by the word 'ascertainment,'
non-knowledge in the form of sense-contact and the like [is excluded];
and doubt and the like, though knowledge-in-form, are denied the status of <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Therein, 'ascertainment' (<s>nirṇaya</s>) is cognition free from doubt, non-determination, and

children.text: अर्यतेऽर्थ्यते वा अर्थो हेयोपादेयोपेक्षणीयलक्षणः, हेयस्य हातुम्, उपादेयस्यो
पादातुम्, उपेक्षणीयस्योपेक्षितुम् अर्थ्यमानत्वात् । न चानुपादेयत्वादुपेक्षणीयो हेय एवा
children.translated_text: what is to be adopted is sought to be adopted, and what is to be ignored is sought to be ignored. Nor does the ignorable fall within the rejectable merely because it is not-to-be-adopted;

children.text: न्तर्भवति; अहेयत्वादुपादेय एवान्तर्भावप्रसक्तेः । उपेक्षणीय एव च मूर्द्धाभिषिक्तोऽर्थः,
children.translated_text: for there would be the unwanted consequence that it falls within the adoptable because it is not-to-be-rejected. The ignorable is indeed the paramount object,
because it is sought by
<s>yogins</s>. And for us too, the ignorable objects far exceed the rejectable and adoptable;
therefore, this [category] cannot be
neglected.

children.text: । अर्थस्य निर्णय इति कर्मणि षष्ठी, निर्णीयमानत्वेन व्याप्यत्वा
children.translated_text: 'Ascertainment of the object' — the genitive is in the objective sense, because the object has the nature of being determined (<s>nirṇīyamāna</s>).

children.text: दर्थस्य । अर्थग्रहणं च स्वनिर्णयव्यवच्छेदार्थं तस्य सतोऽप्यलक्षणत्वादिति वक्ष्यामः ।
children.translated_text: And the word 'object' is for excluding self-ascertainment, since even when it exists, it is not a defining characteristic — as we shall explain.
'Object' (<s>artha</s>) — that which is sought or desired — is characterized as what is to be rejected, adopted, or ignored. What is to be rejected is sought to be rejected,
qualifies 'ascertainment,'
since ascertainment alone is fit to be qualified as correct or incorrect; but the object
is not itself correct or in-
correct — since the possibilities of existence

children.text: व्यभिचारयोरभावान्न विशेषणीयः । तेन सम्यग् योऽर्थनिर्णय इति
children.translated_text: and deviation do not apply [to it], it need not be qualified. Therefore, by qualifying as 'correct ascertainment of the object,'
error is excluded. Thus, this general definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> is free from the faults of over-extension, under-extension, and impossibility. (2)
'Correctly' (<s>samyak</s>) — is an indeclinable meaning 'not contrary,' or a form derived from '<s>samañc</s>.' And it
and what is other [than itself].'
'<s>Pramāṇa</s> [cognizes] itself
(<s>Nyāyāvatāra</s> 1)
is <s>pramāṇa</s>.'
'Cognition that consists of the determination of its own object
(<s>Tattvārthaślokavārttika</s>
And this is not without [basis], since in 'I know the pot,' the cognition too appears [to itself] just as the agent and the object do.

children.text: वसन्, घटमहं जानामि इत्यादौ कर्तृकर्मवत् ज्ञप्तेरप्यवभासमा

children.translated_text: Nor is the perception of an object that is not directly apprehended established [otherwise].

children.text: स्यार्थदृष्टिः प्रसिद्ध्यति । न च ज्ञानान्तरात् तदु
children.translated_text: Nor is the apprehension [of cognition] possible through another cognition,
because that [other cognition] too, being unapprehended, cannot be directly perceived for the present apprehension.
And if another apprehension is posited, there is an infinite regress. If apprehension [of cognition] depends on apprehension of the object, there is the fallacy of mutual dependence. By this,
the occurrence of the object
would not be
possible
unless
cognition existed — even the apprehension [of cognition] through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is refuted; for
that [presumption] too, if unknown,
cannot serve as a means of knowing. If [it is known] through another presumption,
then there is an infinite regress
or mutual dependence —
a defeat in either

children.text: वस्थः परिभवः । तस्मादर्थोन्मुखतयेव स्वोन्मुखतयापि ज्ञानस्य प्रतिभासात् स्वनिर्णया
children.translated_text: case. Therefore, since cognition appears with a self-directed aspect just as it has an object-directed aspect, it too has the nature of self-ascertainment.
Objection: If experience were itself experienced, it would follow that it is not experience, like a pot. Do not speak thus!
For just as the knower [is known] by its nature as knower, so experience is experienced by its very nature as experience.

children.text: ज्ञातुर्ज्ञातृत्वेनेव अनुभूतेरनुभूतित्वेनैवानुभवात् । न चानुभूतेरनुभाव्यत्वं दोषः; अर्थापेक्ष
children.translated_text: Nor is it a fault that experience is experienced; for from the standpoint of the object, it is experience, and from its own standpoint, it is experienced — just as one person is both a son [of his father]

and a father [of his son], and there is no contradiction. Nor is there a contradiction of self-action upon oneself; for since the matter is established by experience, the contradiction is not proven. And through inference too,

children.text: धाभावात् । न च स्वात्मनि क्रियाविरोधः; अनुभवसिद्धेऽर्थे विरोधासिद्धेः । अनुमानाच्च
children.translated_text: self-awareness is established; thus: cognition illuminates an object only when it is itself illuminated, because it is an illuminator, like a lamp.

children.text: स्वसंवेदनसिद्धिः; तथाहि--ज्ञानं प्रकाशमानमेवार्थं प्रकाशयति, प्रकाशकत्वात्, प्रदीपवत् ।

children.translated_text: If [you say] that because awareness is to be illuminated, its being an illuminator is unproven —
no; because its being an illuminator is established through the removal of
ignorance

To this, he responds:
Objection: A <s>pramāṇa</s> that ascertains an already-ascertained object would be grinding what is already ground. And thus,
Just like [cognitions that will] apprehend what is yet to be grasped, even those that grasp the already-grasped are not devoid of validity. (Sūtra 4)

'Rather, its not being born from the object is the cause of its invalidity.'
And memory (<s>smṛti</s>), which is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, has precisely the nature of grasping-the-already-grasped.

children.text: यद्विशदसम्यगर्थनिर्णयात्मकं न भवति न तत् प्रत्यक्षम्, यथा परोक्षमिति व्यतिरेकी ।
children.translated_text: 'That which does not have the nature of a vivid, correct determination of the object is not perception, as for instance indirect knowledge (<s>parokṣa</s>)' — this is the negative concomitance (<s>vyatirekin</s>).

children.text: धर्म्मिणो हेतुत्वेऽनन्वयदोष इति चेत्; न; विशेषे धर्मिणि धर्मिसामान्यस्य हेतुत्वात् ।
children.translated_text: If [one objects that] when the subject itself is the reason, there is the fallacy of non-concomitance (<s>ananvaya</s>) — no, because the subject-universal serves as the reason in a particular subject.

children.text: तस्य च विशेषनिष्ठत्वेन विशेषेष्वन्वयसम्भवात् । सपक्षे वृत्तिमन्तरेणापि च विपक्षव्या
children.translated_text: And since it resides in particulars, concomitance in particulars is possible. Even without occurrence in the positive instances (<s>sapakṣa</s>), probative force [can arise]
through exclusion from the negative instances (<s>vipakṣa</s>) — this has already been stated. (sūtra 13)
By restating the general definition and then prescribing the specific definition: 'a correct determination of the object' is the general definition of a means of knowledge;

children.text: अथ किमिदं वैशद्यं नाम ? । यदि स्वविषयग्रहणम्; तत् परोक्षेप्य

children.translated_text: If it means
'clarity' (<s>sphuṭatva</s>), that too is common to all cognitions since they are all self-known — anticipating this [objection], he says:
Now, what is this 'vividness' (<s>vaiśadya</s>)? If it means 'apprehension of one's own object,' that is undiminished even in indirect knowledge.
'Vividness is [either] non-dependence on other means of knowledge, or appearance as "this".' (sūtra 14)

children.text: प्रस्तुतात् प्रमाणाद् यदन्यत् प्रमाणं शब्दलिङ्गादिज्ञानं तत् प्रमाणान्तरं तन्निर

children.translated_text: on that is vividness. For perception, unlike
verbal testimony, inference, and the like, does not depend for its origination on cognitions of words, marks, etc. as another means of

children.text: न्तरमपेक्षते इत्येकं वैशद्यलक्षणम् । लक्षणान्तरमपि इदन्तया प्रतिभासो वा इति,
children.translated_text: knowledge — this is one definition of vividness. Another definition is also [given]: 'or appearance as "this"' — meaning

children.text: इदन्तया विशेषनिष्ठतया यः प्रतिभासः सम्यगर्थनिर्णयस्य सोऽपि वैशद्यम् । वाशब्दो
children.translated_text: that which is the appearance, i.e., the correct determination of the object, characterized by the particular determination 'this' — that too is vividness. The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>)
indicates that it is an alternative definition. (sūtra 14)
Whatever other means of knowledge is different from the present means — cognitions of words, marks (<s>liṅga</s>), etc. — that is 'another means of knowledge.' Non-dependence

children.text: अथ मुख्यसांव्यवहारिकभेदेन द्वैविध्यं प्रत्यक्षस्य हृदि निधाय मुख्यस्य

children.translated_text: the definition of the principal [perception]:
Now, keeping in mind the twofold nature of perception — the principal (<s>mukhya</s>) and the conventional (<s>sāṃvyavahārika</s>) — he states

children.text: तत् सर्वथावरणविलये चेतनस्य स्वरूपाविर्भावो मुख्यं केवलम् ॥ १५ ॥
children.translated_text: 'That [perception], the manifestation of the soul's own nature upon the complete destruction of all obscurations in the conscious being, is the principal — the absolute (<s>kevala</s>).' (sūtra 15)
otherwise, it would be connected only with the immediately preceding 'vividness.' At the culmination
of the perfection of the three jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>) — cultivated through long, continuous practice
and without interruption — through the power of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) characterized by unity, free from deliberation and reflection,
upon the complete destruction of the destructive <s>karmas</s>

children.text: दीनां घातिकर्मणां प्रक्षये सति चेतनास्वभावस्यात्मनः प्रकाशस्वभावस्येति
children.translated_text: such as the knowledge-obscuring (<s>jñānāvaraṇīya</s>) [karma], of the self (<s>ātman</s>) whose essential nature is consciousness, whose nature is luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) — that is

children.text: यावत्, स्वरूपस्य प्रकाशस्वभावस्य सत एवावरणापगमेन आविर्भावः आविर्भूतं स्वरूपं
children.translated_text: to say, the manifestation of the inherent nature of luminosity, which already exists, through the removal of obscuration — the manifested essential nature,

children.text: मुखमिव शरीरस्य सर्वज्ञानानां प्रधानं मुख्यम् प्रत्यक्षम् । तच्चेन्द्रियादिसाहायकविरहात्
children.translated_text: like the face of the body, being the principal among all cognitions, is the 'principal' (<s>mukhya</s>) perception. And this, because it is devoid of assistance from sense-organs and the like,
because it has all things as its objects, and because it is unique, is 'absolute' (<s>kevala</s>) — thus it is well-known in scripture (<s>āgama</s>).
'That' (<s>tat</s>) is for referring back to perception;

children.text: प्रकाशस्वभावता कथमात्मनः सिद्धेति चेत्; एते ब्रूमः--आत्मा प्रकाशस्व
भावः, असन्दिग्धस्वभावत्वात्, यः प्रकाशस्वभावो न भवति नासावसन्दिग्धस्वभावो यथा
children.translated_text: because its nature is not subject to doubt. Whatever is not of luminous nature is not of undoubted nature, like

children.text: घटः, न च तथात्मा, न खलु कश्चिदहमस्मि न वेति सन्दिग्धे इति नासिद्धो हेतुः । तथा,
children.translated_text: a pot. But the self is not like that — for no one doubts 'do I exist or not?' — so the reason is not unestablished. Likewise,

children.text: आत्मा प्रकाशस्वभावः, बोद्धृत्वात्, यः प्रकाशस्वभावो न भवति नासौ बोद्धा यथा घटः,
children.translated_text: the self is of luminous nature, because it is a knower (<s>boddhṛ</s>). Whatever is not of luminous nature is not a knower, like a pot.

children.text: न च न बोद्धात्मेति । तथा, यो यस्याः क्रियायाः कर्त्ता न स तद्विषयो यथा गतिक्रिया
children.translated_text: And the self is not a non-knower. Likewise: whoever is the agent of a certain action is not the object of that action — just as <s>Caitra</s>, who is the agent of the action of going,

children.text: याः कर्त्ता चैत्रो न तद्विषयः, ज्ञप्तिक्रियायाः कर्ता चात्मेति ।
children.translated_text: is not the object of that [going]; and the self is the agent of the action of knowing.
If [one asks] how the luminous nature of the self is established — we say: The self is of luminous nature,

children.text: अथ प्रकाशस्वभावत्व आत्मनः कथमावरणम् ?, आवरणे वा सततावरणप्र
सङ्गः; नैवम्; प्रकाशस्वभावस्यापि चन्द्रार्कादेरिव रजोनीहाराभ्रपटलादिभिरिव ज्ञाना
children.translated_text: without end? — No, it is not so; because even for things of luminous nature, like the moon and sun, obscuration by dust, mist, clouds, and the like is possible — similarly, obscuration by
knowledge-obscuring and other <s>karmas</s> [is possible]. And like the moon and
sun, through powerful purifying agents
such as meditation, contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
and the like, destruction [of obscuration is possible]
— thus.
Now, if the self has a luminous nature, how can there be obscuration? And in the case of obscuration, wouldn't there be perpetual obscuration

children.text: ननु सादित्वे स्यादावरणस्योपायतो विलयः; नैवम्; अनादेरपि सुवर्णम

children.translated_text: alkali, earth, crucible-firing, and the like is observed; likewise, even for the beginningless knowledge-obscuring and other <s>karmas</s>,
destruction through the practice of the three jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>), which is their counteragent, is logically established.
Objection: Only if the obscuration had a beginning would its destruction through a means [be possible]. — No, it is not so; because even of the beginningless impurity of gold, destruction through

children.text: न चामूर्त्तस्यात्मनः कथमावरणमिति वाच्यम्; अमूर्ताया अपि चेतनाशक्ते

children.translated_text: obscuration by liquor, intoxicants, <s>kodrava</s> (a type of millet), and the like is observed.
And one should not say 'how can there be obscuration of the immaterial (<s>amūrta</s>) self?' — because even of the immaterial consciousness-power (<s>cetanā-śakti</s>),

children.text: अथावरणीयतत्प्रतिपक्षाभ्यामात्मा विक्रियेत न वा ? । किं चातः ? ।

children.translated_text: 'What [effect] have rain and sun on space? On leather, there is [indeed] their effect.
If [the self] is like leather, then it is impermanent; if like space, then the effect is unreal.'

children.text: इति चेत्; न; अस्य दूषणस्य कूटस्थनित्यतापक्ष एव सम्भवात्, परिणामिनित्यश्चात्मेति
children.translated_text: — If [this be objected], no; because this objection applies only to the position of absolute permanence (<s>kūṭasthanityatā</s>). The self is permanent-through-transformation (<s>pariṇāminityā</s>),
because its nature consists of continuity accompanied by origination and destruction in successive
temporal stages — since in the positions of absolute permanence and momentariness (<s>kṣaṇika</s>),
there is the complete absence of purposive action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) in every respect. As has been said:
'Purposive action is not possible in either the permanent or the momentary position;
<s>Laghīyastraya</s> 2.1.
that [purposive action], the defining characteristic of things, [operates] through both sequence and non-sequence.'
Thus. (sūtra 15)
Now, is the self modified by the obscuring [karma] and its counteragent, or not? — And what of it?

children.text: ननु प्रमाणाधीना प्रमेयव्यवस्था । न च मुख्यप्रत्यक्षस्य तद्वतो वा सिद्धौ

children.translated_text: there is no means of knowledge whatsoever. For perception, its operation being restricted to objects such as form and the like,
is unable to engage with a supersensory
object. Nor [can] inference [establish it], since inference is of the nature of being produced through the power of the connection between the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the marked (<s>liṅgin</s>)
that has been
seen by perception.
As for scripture (<s>āgama</s>): if it is based on supersensory knowledge, then it can establish that; but this is mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>) —
<s>Ślokavārtika</s>, sūtra 2, verse 142.
'Without that scripture, [the supersensory knowledge] cannot be established; nor can the scripture [be established] without it.'
And an authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) [scripture] that could establish that simply does not exist. Even the [verse]:
without feet, yet

children.text: अत्र जवनो इत्येव सम्यक्, तस्यैव शङ्करेण व्याख्यातत्वात् ।

children.translated_text: swift, the seizer; he sees without eyes, he hears without ears.
'Without hands,

children.text: न हि तस्य वेत्ता तमाहुरग्र्यं पुरुषं महान्तम् ॥
children.translated_text: yet there is no knower of him — they call him the foremost, the great <s>Puruṣa</s>.'
<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 3.19.
He knows the universe,

children.text: इत्यादिः कश्चिदर्थवादरूपोऽस्ति नासौ प्रमाणम् विधावेव प्रामाण्योपगमात् । प्रमाणान्त
children.translated_text: — this and such [passages] are of the nature of laudatory statements (<s>arthavāda</s>), not a means of knowledge, since validity is accepted only in injunctive [statements]. And since other means
of knowledge have no scope here at all — anticipating this, he says:
Objection: The determination of the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) depends on the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). And for the establishment of principal perception, or of one who possesses it,
'Its establishment is [achieved] through the establishment [known from] the culmination of the gradation of wisdom, etc.' (sūtra 16)

children.text: शयवदित्यनुमानेन निरतिशयप्रज्ञासिद्ध्या तस्य केवलज्ञानस्य सिद्धिः, तत्सिद्धिरूपत्वात्
children.translated_text: By this inference, through the establishment of unsurpassed wisdom, the establishment of that absolute knowledge (<s>kevalajñāna</s>) [is achieved] — since the establishment of absolute knowledge has the nature of that [unsurpassed wisdom].

children.text: केवलज्ञानसिद्धेः । आदिग्रहणात् सूक्ष्मान्तरितदूरार्थाः कस्यचित् प्रत्यक्षाः प्रमेयत्वात्
children.translated_text: From the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>): subtle, hidden, and distant objects are directly perceptible to someone, because they are knowable, like a pot.
From this, and from the consistency of astronomical knowledge, and from the impossibility of explaining it otherwise — its establishment [follows]. As has been said:
The gradation — hierarchy — of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) must culminate somewhere, because it is a gradation, like the gradation of size.

children.text: धीरत्यन्तपरोक्षेऽर्थे न चेत् पुंसां कुतः पुनः ।
children.translated_text: 'If people had no cognition of objects that are extremely remote [from the senses], then whence
<s>Siddhiviniscaya</s>, p. 413A.
the consistency of astronomical knowledge? And if [one says] "from scripture" — then [there must be] another means [beyond scripture].'

children.text: नोदना हि भूतं भवन्तं भविष्यन्तं सूक्ष्मं व्यवहितं विप्र

children.translated_text: and distant — and nothing else [does so] — no other sense-organ' —
'Injunction (<s>nōdanā</s>) makes known objects that are past, present, future, subtle, concealed,
<s>Śābara Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.2.

children.text: इति वदता भूताद्यर्थपरिज्ञानं कस्यचित् पुंसोऽभिमतमेव, अन्यथा कस्मै वेदस्त्रिकालविषय
children.translated_text: — by saying this, it is acknowledged that the knowledge of past and other objects belongs to some person; otherwise, to whom would the <s>Veda</s> communicate the object
pertaining to the three times? For in communicating, it accepts as its qualified recipient only one who knows the reality pertaining to the three times. As has been said:
'To whom would the <s>Veda</s> communicate the reality pertaining to the three times
<s>Siddhiviniscaya</s>, p. 414A.
if no person knows it thus, [being] exclusively [bound by] inexhaustible obscurations?'
Thus, from the impossibility of otherwise explaining the communication of the reality pertaining to the three times, the establishment of supersensory absolute knowledge [is achieved].
Moreover:

children.text: य एव हि शास्त्रस्य विषयः स्याद्वादः स एव प्रत्यक्षादेरपीति संवादः, तथाहि-
children.translated_text: For the very subject of scripture — the <s>syādvāda</s> (the doctrine of conditional predication) — is also [the subject] of perception and the like; thus there is concordance. For example:
'Everything exists in its own nature; in another's nature, it does not exist.
Otherwise, everything would exist [in everything], and even one's own nature would be impossible.'

children.text: इति दिशा प्रमाणसिद्धं स्याद्वादं प्रतिपादयन्नागमोऽर्हतस्सर्वज्ञतामपि प्रतिपादयति,
children.translated_text: Thus, the scripture (<s>āgama</s>), by teaching the <s>syādvāda</s> that is established by means of knowledge in [this] manner, also teaches the omniscience of the <s>Arhat</s> (the Jina).
As has been expressed:
'By the power of whose right faith we understand the supreme-self-nature of ones like you —
<s>Ayogavyavaccheda</s> [verse] 21.
for the destruction of the bonds of evil dispositions — salutation be to that teaching of yours!'
And though perception, being sensory,
does not have supersensory knowledge as its object, nevertheless, yogic perception (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>), born from the power of meditative concentration (<s>samādhi</s>),

children.text: योगिप्रत्यक्षमेव बाह्यार्थस्येव स्वस्यापि वेदकमिति प्रत्यक्षतोऽपि तत्सिद्धिः ।
children.translated_text: knows both external objects and itself — thus, from perception too, its establishment [is achieved].

Furthermore, scripture itself, which is concordant with what is established by perception and inference, is the means of knowledge for [establishing] the existence of one who sees supersensory objects.
and detachment, belonging to the Lord of the world,
'Knowledge that is unobstructed,
sovereignty and <s>dharma</s> — [these are] the fourfold [qualities] that are innately accomplished.'

children.text: इति वचनात्सर्वज्ञत्वमीश्वरादीनामस्तु मानुषस्य तु कस्यचिद्विद्याचरणवतोपि तदसम्भाव
children.translated_text: — From this statement, let omniscience belong to <s>Īśvara</s> and the like; but for some human being, even one endowed with learning and conduct, it is
inconceivable. As <s>Kumārila</s> [says]:
'Even granting that <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>, having <s>Vedic</s> bodies,

children.text: कामं भवन्तु सर्वज्ञाः सार्वज्ञ्यं मानुषस्य किम् ? ॥

children.translated_text: <s>Tattvasaṃgraha</s>-
<s>Tattvasaṃgraha</s>-
<s>kārikā</s> 3208.
may be omniscient — what [use is] omniscience for a human being?'

children.text: इति; आः ! सर्वज्ञापलापपातकिन् ! दुर्वदवादिन् ! मानुषत्वनिन्दार्थवादापदेशेन देवाधि
children.translated_text: — Ha! O sinner who denies omniscience! O speaker of vile words! Under the pretext of a laudatory statement disparaging human nature, you deprecate

children.text: देवानधिक्षिपसि ? । ये हि जन्मान्तरार्ज्जितोर्जितपुण्यप्राग्भाराः सुरभवभवमनुपमं सुख
children.translated_text: the Gods of Gods! Those who, bearing the preponderant mass of merit acquired in previous births, having experienced the incomparable bliss of celestial existence,

children.text: मनुभूय दुःखपङ्कमग्नमखिलं जीवलोकमुद्दिधीर्षवो नरकेष्वपि क्षणं क्षिप्तसुखासिकामृत
children.translated_text: desiring to lift up the entire world of souls submerged in the mire of suffering, [those who,] even in the hells, showering nectar from the instantly-drawn sword of bliss,
descended to the human world — [those] whose birth-festivals were performed by all the hosts of divine lords who rose from their seats at the very moment of [their] birth,
whose service was undertaken by throngs of celestial beings vying with each other in eager rivalry; [who,]

rejecting like grass the supremely abundant imperial sovereignty that came of its own accord, equal in their regard for straw and jewel, enemy and friend, [who,] having pacified through their own power the worldly calamities

children.text: स्वचक्रं परचक्रं च सप्तैता ईतयः स्मृताः ॥ --मु--टि॰

children.translated_text: of <s>Iti</s>-
<s>Mara</s> (famine, epidemic), etc. —

[who,] having burnt the destructive <s>karmas</s> in the fire of pure meditation (<s>śukla-dhyāna</s>), [whose] absolute [knowledge] (<s>kevala</s>), manifesting the nature of being and non-being of all things, dispelled by its power

the spread of delusion in the entire world of souls — [who,] having ascended the <s>samavasaraṇa</s> (holy assembly-ground) constructed by gods and demons, [who,] with speeches that transform into each being's own language,
established the ford of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmatīrtha</s>) — [who,] having enjoyed the glory of being a <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s>

children.text: साग्रे च गव्यूतिशतद्वये रुजा वैरेतयो मार्यतिवृष्ट्यवृष्टयः ।
खे धर्मचक्रं चमराः सपादपीठं मृगेन्द्रासनमुज्ज्वलं च ।

children.translated_text: comprising thirty-four extraordinary qualities,
attained the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, eternal bliss, complete release from all <s>karmas</s> — you disparage them by teaching that they share ordinary attributes like human nature! You might as well

children.translated_text: reduce even <s>Sumeru</s> to the commonplace by saying it is 'earthen'! Moreover, [do you claim] the empire of omniscience for <s>Brahmā</s> and the others — those who are engaged in

anger, greed, and delight —

Thus, the falsity would be imputed only to the narratives of the <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and <s>Itihāsas</s> concerning deities such as <s>Brahmā</s> and others.
Thus, the establishment of supersensory knowledge (<s>atīndriya-jñāna</s>) from the valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that serve as provers has been stated. (17)
Now —
And because there is no invalidator (<s>bādhaka</s>). (17)

children.translated_text: invalidator is impossible, its establishment is [certain], like pleasure and the like — thus the connection [of the sūtra is understood]. Namely:

children.text: केवलज्ञानबाधकं भवत् प्रत्यक्षं वा भवेत् प्रमाणान्तरं वा ? । न तावत् प्रत्यक्षम्; तस्य
children.translated_text: Would the invalidator of [supersensory] knowledge be perception or another means of knowledge? It is not perception, to begin with; since perception
has its scope only in what is present —
[Reference:] <s>Ślokavārttika</s>, Sūtra 4, Śloka 84.
'What is connected and present is grasped by the eye and the like.'
— since he himself has stated this.
Since a well-ascertained

children.text: अथ न प्रवर्तमानं प्रत्यक्षं तद्बाधकं किन्तु निवर्तमानम् तत्; त

children.translated_text: then:
If

children.text: नियतदेशकालविषयत्वेन बाधकं तर्हि सम्प्रतिपद्यामहे । अथ सकलदेशकालविषयत्वेन;
children.translated_text: it invalidates with respect to a specific place, time, and object, then we accept [that limited invalidation]. But if [it claims to invalidate] with respect to all places, times, and objects,
then that is not possible without direct realization by all persons of all places and times

— thus our intended [conclusion] is established. And neither <s>Jaimini</s> nor anyone else can be a direct perceiver of all places and the like, because of possessing existence, personhood, and similar [limitations],

children.text: हितम् । न च जैमिनिरन्यो वा सकलदेशादिसाक्षात्कारी सम्भवति सत्त्वपुरुषत्वादेः
children.translated_text: just like an ordinary person on the street. Now, if because intelligence admits of degrees, its highest degree is also inferred; then from that very [premise], why is not an all-seeing being also inferred?

children.text: रथ्यापुरुषवत् । अथ प्रज्ञायाः सातिशयत्वात्तत्प्रकर्षोऽप्यनुमीयते; तर्हि तत एव सकलार्थ
children.translated_text: And indeed, [the opponent,] while not treating non-apprehension as a valid proof in his own position [regarding denying omniscience],

children.text: दर्शी किं नानुमीयते ? । स्वपक्षे चानुपलम्भमप्रमाणयन् सर्वज्ञाभावे कुतः प्रमाणयेद
children.translated_text: how would he treat it as a valid proof for the non-existence of an omniscient being,
especially?
Now, if it is not active perception that invalidates, but rather ceased [past] perception;

children.text: न चानुमानं तद्बाधकं सम्भवति; धर्मिग्रहणमन्तरेणानुमानाप्रवृत्तेः, धर्म्मि

children.translated_text: then inference itself does not arise, because it would be invalidated by the very means of knowledge that grasps the subject. Now, if one argues: 'The person under dispute

children.text: सर्वज्ञो न भवति वक्तृत्वात् पुरुषत्वाद्वा रथ्यापुरुषवदित्यनुमानं तद्बाधकं ब्रूषे; तदसत्;
children.translated_text: is not omniscient because of being a speaker, or because of being a person, like an ordinary person on the street' — that this inference invalidates [omniscience]; that is wrong.

children.text: यतो यदि प्रमाणपरिदृष्टार्थवक्तृत्वं हेतुः; तदा विरुद्धः, तादृशस्य वक्तृत्वस्य सर्वज्ञ एव
children.translated_text: Because if 'being a speaker of objects seen through valid means of knowledge' is the reason, then it is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), since such speakership exists only

in an omniscient being. And if 'speaking of non-existent things' [is the reason], then it proves what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>), since those who speak things contradicted by valid means are already accepted as non-omniscient.

children.text: त्वात् । वक्तृत्वमात्रं तु सन्दिग्धविपक्षव्यावृत्तिकत्वादनैकान्तिकम् ज्ञानप्रकर्षे वक्तृत्वाप
children.translated_text: Mere speakership, however, is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because its exclusion from the counter-example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is doubtful — since no decrease in speakership is observed with increase in knowledge;

children.text: कर्षादर्शनात्, प्रत्युत ज्ञानातिशयवतो वक्तृत्वातिशयस्यैवोपलब्धेः । एतेन पुरुषत्वमपि
children.translated_text: on the contrary, increased speakership is observed in one with superior knowledge. By this, [the reason of] 'personhood' is also refuted.

children.text: निरस्तम् । पुरुषत्वं हि यदि रागाद्यदूषितं तदा विरुद्धम्, ज्ञानवैराग्यादिगुणयुक्तपुरुषत्वस्य
children.translated_text: For if personhood means [that which is] untainted by passion and the like, then it is contradictory, since personhood endowed with the qualities of knowledge, dispassion, and the like

children.text: सर्वज्ञतामन्तरेणानुपपत्तेः । रागादिदूषिते तु पुरुषत्वे सिद्धसाध्यता । पुरुषत्वसामान्यं तु
children.translated_text: is impossible without omniscience. But if personhood tainted by passion and the like [is meant], then it proves what is already established. And mere personhood in general
has doubtful exclusion from the counter-example, and hence is not an invalidator.
Nor can inference be its invalidator; because without grasping the subject (<s>dharmin</s>), inference does not operate. Or if the subject is grasped,
no such invalidating [scripture] is seen. And how can a scripture whose author is an omniscient being
invalidate that [omniscience] itself? Enough with this excessive digression. (17)
Nor is scripture (<s>āgama</s>) an invalidator of that, because an authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) [scripture invalidating omniscience] is impossible; or even if possible,

children.text: न केवलं केवलमेव मुख्यं प्रत्यक्षमपि त्वन्यदपीत्याह--
children.translated_text: Not only <s>kevala</s> (omniscient) [knowledge] is primary direct perception, but there are others too — he says:
<s>Avadhi</s> (clairvoyance) and <s>manaḥparyāya</s> (telepathy) are [primary direct perception] when there is a gradation in that [removal of karmic obstruction].

children.text: पशमविशेषे तन्निमित्तकः अवधिः अवधिज्ञानं मनःपर्यायः मनःपर्यायज्ञानं च मुख्य
children.translated_text: that is, in the particular destruction-cum-subsidence of the obstruction — the result is <s>avadhi</s>, i.e., <s>avadhi</s>-knowledge, and <s>manaḥparyāya</s>, i.e., <s>manaḥparyāya</s>-knowledge — [these are also] primary,

children.text: मिन्द्रियानपेक्षं प्रत्यक्षम् । तत्रावधीयत इति अवधिः मर्यादा सा च
children.translated_text: sense-independent direct perception. There, '<s>avadhi</s>' [means] 'that by which something is limited' — i.e., a boundary. And that
'Clairvoyance [applies to] material things' —
[Reference:] <s>Tattvārtha</s> 1.28.

children.text: इति वचनात् रूपवद्द्रव्यविषया अवध्युपलक्षितं ज्ञानमप्यवधिः । स द्वेधा
children.translated_text: — as stated, it has as its object material (<s>rūpavat</s>) substances. The knowledge delimited by <s>avadhi</s> is also [called] <s>avadhi</s>. It is of two kinds:

children.translated_text: <s>bhavapratyaya</s> (birth-born) and <s>guṇapratyaya</s> (quality-born). Of these, the first belongs to gods and hell-beings, like birds' ability to fly through the sky. The quality-born
belongs to humans and animals.
When the obstruction is completely removed, [there is] <s>kevala</s> (omniscience). When there is a gradation in that removal of obstruction —

children.text: मनसो द्रव्यरूपस्य पर्यायाश्चिन्तनानुगुणाः परिणामभेदास्तद्विषयं ज्ञानं मनः
पर्यायः । तथाविधमनःपर्यायान्यथानुपपत्त्या तु यद्बाह्यचिन्तनीयार्थज्ञानं तत् आनुमानिक
children.translated_text: (telepathy). However, knowledge of external thinkable objects [inferred] by the impossibility of [explaining] such <s>manaḥparyāya</s> otherwise is merely inferential,
not <s>manaḥparyāya</s> direct perception. As they say:

The <s>paryāyas</s> (modifications) of the mind (<s>manas</s>), which is a material substance, are transformations corresponding to thought — knowledge having those as its object is <s>manaḥparyāya</s>
[Reference:] <s>Viśeṣāvaśyaka</s>, Gāthā 814.
Thus.
Thus. (18)
'One knows the external through inference.'

children.translated_text: — he says:

Now, since both have in common the features of having material substances as their object and being due to destruction-cum-subsidence [of karma], what is the difference between <s>avadhi</s> and <s>manaḥparyāya</s>?
Their difference is due to differences in purity, field, possessor, and object. (19)

children.text: तत्रावधिज्ञानान्मनःपर्यायज्ञानं विशुद्धतरम् । यानि हि मनोद्रव्याणि अवधिज्ञानी
children.translated_text: There, <s>manaḥparyāya</s>-knowledge is purer than <s>avadhi</s>-knowledge. For those mental substances that the <s>avadhi</s>-knower
knows, the <s>manaḥparyāya</s>-knower knows them in a purer form.
Even though there is some similarity, the difference between <s>avadhi</s>-knowledge and <s>manaḥparyāya</s>-knowledge is due to differences in purity and the like.
— <s>avadhi</s>-knowledge operates from an innumerable fraction of an <s>aṅgula</s> (finger-breadth) up to the entire

children.text: लोकात्, मनःपर्यायज्ञानं तु मनुष्यक्षेत्र एव भवति ।
children.translated_text: universe; <s>manaḥparyāya</s>-knowledge, however, operates only in the human realm.
As for the difference in field (<s>kṣetra</s>):

children.text: भवति; मनःपर्यायज्ञानं तु मनुष्यसंयतस्य प्रकृष्टचारित्रस्य प्रमत्तादिषु क्षीणकषायान्तेषु
children.translated_text: <s>manaḥparyāya</s>-knowledge, however, occurs for a restrained human of advanced conduct, in the spiritual stages (<s>guṇasthānaka</s>) from the heedful (<s>pramatta</s>) onward up to the destruction of <s>kaṣāyas</s> (passions).

children.text: गुणस्थानकेषु भवति । तत्रापि वर्धमानपरिणामस्य नेतरस्य । वर्धमानपरिणामस्यापि
children.translated_text: And among those too, only for one of increasing [spiritual] transformation, not for another. And among those with increasing transformation too,
only for one who has attained supernatural accomplishment (<s>ṛddhi</s>), not for another. And among those who have attained accomplishment too, for some, not for all.

The difference in possessor (<s>svāmin</s>): <s>avadhi</s>-knowledge occurs for the restrained (<s>saṃyata</s>), the unrestrained (<s>asaṃyata</s>), and the partially restrained, in all states of existence (<s>gati</s>);
in an infinite fraction
of those, <s>manaḥparyāya</s> [has its range]. Thus concludes [the discussion of] primary direct perception. (19)
The difference in object (<s>viṣaya</s>): <s>avadhi</s> has its range in material substances but not in all their modifications (<s>paryāya</s>);
Now he states conventional [perception]:

Conventional [perception] has the sense-organs and mind as its cause, and consists of <s>avagraha</s> (sensation), <s>īhā</s> (speculation), <s>avāya</s> (judgment), and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (retention). (20)

children.text: इन्द्रियाणि स्पर्शनादीनि वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणानि, मनश्च निमित्तं कारणं यस्य स
तथा । सामान्यलक्षणानुवृत्तेः सम्यगर्थनिर्णयस्येदं विशेषणं तेन इन्द्रियमनोनिमित्तः
children.translated_text: Since the general definition of 'correct determination of an object' continues [here], this is its specification: thus, 'correct determination of an object caused by the sense-organs and mind.'
Having stated the cause, he states the nature: 'consisting of <s>avagraha</s>, <s>īhā</s>, <s>avāya</s>, and <s>dhāraṇā</s>.' <s>Avagraha</s> and the rest

children.text: वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणाः त आत्मा यस्य सोऽवग्रहेहावायधारणात्मा । आत्मग्रहणं च क्रमेणो
children.translated_text: have the characteristics to be described; that whose nature (<s>ātman</s>) they are is 'consisting of <s>avagraha</s>, <s>īhā</s>, <s>avāya</s>, and <s>dhāraṇā</s>.' And the word '<s>ātman</s>' (nature) is used to show that

children.text: त्पद्यमानानामप्यवग्रहादीनां नात्यन्तिको भेदः किन्तु पूर्वपूर्वस्योत्तरोत्तररूपतया परिणा
children.translated_text: even though <s>avagraha</s> and the rest arise in sequence, the difference [between them] is not absolute, but rather, since each earlier [stage] transforms into each later form,

children.text: मादेकात्मकत्वमिति प्रदर्शनार्थम् । समीचीनः प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिरूपो व्यवहारः संव्यवहार
children.translated_text: they are essentially one. Proper activity and cessation constituting practical conduct (<s>vyavahāra</s>) — that is <s>saṃvyavahāra</s>;

children.text: स्तत्प्रयोजनं सांव्यवहारिकम् प्रत्यक्षम् । इन्द्रियमनोनिमित्तत्वं च समस्तं व्यस्तं च
children.translated_text: that which serves as its purpose is <s>sāṃvyavahārika</s> (conventional) perception. And 'being caused by sense-organs and mind' should be understood

children.text: बोद्धव्यम् । इन्द्रियप्राधान्यात् मनोबलाधानाच्चोत्पद्यमान इन्द्रियजः । मनस एव विशुद्धि
children.translated_text: both collectively and distributively. That which arises from the predominance of a sense-organ with the supplementary power of mind is sense-born. That which arises
from the mind itself, with the assistance of its purification, is mind-caused.
The sense-organs — touch and the rest — have the characteristics to be described; and the mind is the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) of that [perception].

children.text: ननु स्वसंवेदनरूपमन्यदपि प्रत्यक्षमस्ति तत् कस्मान्नोक्तम् ?, इति न

children.translated_text: be asked; because the self-awareness of sense-born knowledge
is included in sense-perception; the awareness
of non-sense-born [experiences like] pleasure and the like is included in mental

children.text: प्रत्यक्षे, योगिप्रत्यक्षस्वसंवेदनस्य योगिप्रत्यक्षेऽन्तर्भावात् । स्मृत्यादिस्वसंवेदनं तु मान
children.translated_text: perception; and the self-awareness of yogic perception is included in yogic perception. And the self-awareness of memory and the like is merely [valid] knowledge (<s>māna</s>);

children.text: समेवेति नापरं स्वसंवेदनं नाम प्रत्यक्षमस्तीति भेदेन
children.translated_text: thus there is no separate perception called 'self-awareness' — hence it was
not mentioned separately. (20)
Now, is there not yet another perception in the form of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>)? Why is it not mentioned? — This need not
Having said 'sense-organs,' he now defines the sense-organs:
and auditory organ; they differ as substance and disposition

children.text: इत्यन्तमेकं भेदानि इत्यन्तं च अपरम् इति सूत्रद्वयं

children.translated_text: (i.e., physical organ and its capacity). (21)
The sense-organs, characterized by the apprehension of touch, taste, smell, form, and sound, are the tactile organ, gustatory organ, olfactory organ, visual organ,

children.text: स्पर्शादिग्रहणं लक्षणं येषां तानि यथासङ्ख्यं स्पर्शनादीनीन्द्रियाणि, तथाहि

children.translated_text: The apprehension of touch and the like requires an instrument, being an action — like the action of cutting.
Therein, by the action of <s>Indra</s> [i.e., the self],
therein, by the action of <s>Indra</s>,
the sense-organs are produced —

children.text: नामकर्मोदयनिमित्तत्वात् । इन्द्रस्यात्मनो लिङ्गानि वा, कर्ममलीमसस्य हि स्वयमर्थानु
children.translated_text: because their cause is the fruition of <s>nāmakarma</s> (name-determining karma). Or, they are the signs (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>Indra</s>, i.e., the self: for the self, being stained by karmic impurity, is itself unable
to apprehend objects; the sense-organs are the instruments for the self's apprehension of objects.
Those whose defining characteristic is the apprehension of touch and the like are, correspondingly, the tactile organ and the rest. Namely:
And thus, if the sign is not recognized, inference would not arise; and if it is known through inference, an infinite regress would follow. Not so; because the dispositional
sense-organ (<s>bhāvendriya</s>) is self-known, there is no room for an infinite regress. Or alternatively, 'the signs of <s>Indra</s> (the self), i.e., indicators of the self'
are the sense-organs —
because the instrument is observed to be governed by an agent, just like an axe and the like.
Objection: In that case, the self's knowledge of objects, arising from the sense-organ as a sign (<s>liṅga</s>), would be inferential.

children.text: तानि च द्रव्यभावरूपेण भिद्यन्ते । तत्र द्रव्येन्द्रियाणि नामकर्मोदयनिमि

children.translated_text: while the disposition-organs have as their cause the destruction-cum-subsidence of the relevant obscuring and obstructing [karmas]. This is the five-fold system:

children.text: स्पर्शग्रहणलक्षणं स्पर्शनेन्द्रियं, रसग्रहणलक्षणं रसनेन्द्रियमित्यादि । सकलसंसारिषु भावा
children.translated_text: the tactile organ has the characteristic of apprehending touch; the gustatory organ has the characteristic of apprehending taste — and so on. Among all worldly beings, because the tactile organ is present in all [beings] and

children.text: च्छरीरव्यापकत्वाच्च स्पर्शनस्य पूर्वं निर्देशः, ततः क्रमेणाल्पाल्पजीवविषयत्वाद्रसनघ्राण
children.translated_text: pervades the entire body, it is mentioned first; then, in order, the gustatory, olfactory,
visual, and auditory organs [are mentioned], as they belong to progressively fewer classes of beings.

And these are differentiated as substance-organs (<s>dravyendriya</s>) and disposition-organs (<s>bhāvendriya</s>). Of these, the substance-organs have as their cause the fruition of <s>nāmakarma</s>,
whose remaining sense-obscurations are [still present]. And their [sentience] is established
'Earth [beings] have a mind-duration in between' —
[Reference:] <s>Daśavaikālika</s> 4.1.
— from this authoritative scripture (<s>āptāgama</s>). And from inference: knowledge in some self possesses an ultimate minimum [degree],

children.text: अपकृष्यमाणविशेषत्वात् परिमाणवत्, यत्र तदपकर्षपर्यन्तस्त एकेन्द्रियाः स्थावराः ।
children.translated_text: because it is of a nature that admits of diminishing gradations, like spatial extension. Where that minimum degree is reached — those are one-sensed beings, the stationary ones.

children.text: न च स्पर्शनेन्द्रियस्याप्यभावे भस्मादिषु ज्ञानस्यापकर्षो युक्तः । तत्र हि ज्ञानस्याभाव
children.translated_text: And it is not proper [to say] that even without the tactile sense-organ, the minimum of knowledge would apply to ashes and the like. For in those, there is a complete absence of knowledge,

children.text: एव न पुनरपकर्षस्ततो यथा गगनपरिमाणादारभ्यापकृष्यमाणविशेषं परिमाणं परमाणौ
children.translated_text: not a minimum degree. Just as spatial extension, beginning from the expanse of space and undergoing progressive diminution, reaches its ultimate minimum in the atom,
so too knowledge, beginning from <s>kevala</s>-knowledge (omniscience) and undergoing progressive diminution, is maximally diminished in one-sensed beings.

children.text: कृष्यते । पृथिव्यादीनां च प्रत्येकं जीवत्वसिद्धिरग्रे वक्ष्यते । स्पर्शनरसनेन्द्रिये कृमि
children.translated_text: The proof that earth and the like are individually ensouled (<s>jīva</s>) will be stated later. The tactile and gustatory sense-organs [belong to] worms,
legless insects, centipedes, earthworms, conches, oysters, snails, leeches, and the like — mobile beings [with two senses]. The tactile,
gustatory, and olfactory [organs belong to] ants, termites,
red ants, lice, bedbugs,
flea
s, seed
-cotton-bone-centipede
-spider-grass-leaf-and-wood-carrying [insects] and the like [with three senses]. The tactile, gustatory, olfactory, and visual [organs belong to] bees, wasps, deer-flies,
flies,
mosquitoes,
gnats, mosquitoes, scorpions, <s>nandyāvarta</s> (spiral) insects, beetles, moths, and the like [with four senses]. Together with the auditory [organ], those [five senses belong to]
fish, reptiles, serpents, birds, quadrupeds — all born from animal wombs — and also to all hell-beings, humans, and gods.
The tactile sense-organ, arising from the destruction-cum-subsidence of its [karmic] obscuration, belongs to the stationary beings (<s>sthāvara</s>) — earth, water, fire, wind, and plants —
respectively,
are also sense-organs — so say the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>. Then how are there only five sense-organs? — No; because here only those that are causes of specific types of knowledge
are treated
as sense-organs. If sense-organ-hood were attributed to causes of specific types of action, an infinity of sense-organs would follow,
since specific types of action are infinite. Therefore, from explicit enumeration, there are only five sense-organs.
Objection: The organs characterized by speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals, whose purposes are speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure
and there may be difference (<s>bheda</s>) from the perspective of mode (<s>paryāyārtha</s>). For if non-difference alone [were the case],

children.text: दैकान्ते हि स्पर्शनेन स्पर्शस्येव रसादेरपि ग्रहणप्रसङ्गः । तथाचेन्द्रियान्तरकल्पना वैयर्थ्यम्,
children.translated_text: the tactile organ would apprehend not only touch but also taste and the like — a fallacy. And then the postulation of other sense-organs would be pointless;

children.text: कस्यचित् साकल्ये वैकल्ये वान्येषां साकल्यवैकल्यप्रसङ्गश्च । भेदैकान्तेऽपि तेषामेक
children.translated_text: and if one [sense-organ] were complete or deficient, all others would also be complete or deficient — a fallacy. Even if difference alone [were the case], the impossibility
of those [sense-organs]
together

generating a unified knowledge would follow, just like sense-organs belonging to another continuum (<s>santāna</s>). If [one says] the mind (<s>manas</s>) is the generator of that [unified knowledge];

children.text: मिति चेत्; न; तस्येन्द्रियनिरपेक्षस्य तज्जनकत्वाभावात् । इन्द्रियापेक्षं मनोऽनुसन्धानस्य
children.translated_text: no; because the mind, being independent of sense-organs [in that scenario], would not be the generator. If [one says] the mind generates the synthesis (<s>anusandhāna</s>) while depending on sense-organs;

children.text: जनकमिति चेत्; सन्तानान्तरेन्द्रियापेक्षस्य कुतो न जनकत्वमिति वाच्यम् ? । प्रत्यासत्ते
children.translated_text: then why would it not equally be the generator when depending on sense-organs of another continuum? If [one says] because of the absence of proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>);

children.text: रभावादिति चेत्; अत्र का प्रत्यासत्तिरन्यत्रैकद्रव्यतादात्म्यात् ?, प्रत्यासत्त्यन्तरस्य
children.translated_text: then what proximity is there here other than identity with one substance (<s>ekadravya-tādātmya</s>)? And because any other [type of] proximity
is

children.text: व्यभिचारादिति । एतेन तेषामात्मना भेदाभेदैकान्तौ प्रतिव्यूढौ । आत्मना करणानाम
children.translated_text: subject to deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). By this, the one-sided views of absolute identity and absolute difference of these [sense-organs] with the self are also refuted. If there is absolute non-difference of the instruments [sense-organs] from the self,

children.text: भेदैकान्ते कर्तृत्वप्रसङ्गः, आत्मनो वा करणत्वप्रसङ्गः, उभयोरुभयात्मकत्वप्रसङ्गो वा,
children.translated_text: then the self would become an instrument; or the instruments would become the agent — or both would have the nature of both;

children.text: विशेषाभावात् । ततस्तेषां भेदैकान्ते चात्मनः करणत्वाभावः सन्तानान्तरकरणवद्विपर्ययो
children.translated_text: because there would be no distinguishing feature. Hence, if there is absolute difference of these [from the self], there would be no instrumentality for the self, just like instruments of another continuum — or
vice versa. Therefore, since this is established by experience and there is no invalidator, <s>anekānta</s> (non-one-sidedness) alone must be adopted.
And among themselves, there may be non-difference (<s>abheda</s>) from the perspective of substance (<s>dravyārtha</s>),
alone is proper, because both non-difference from the perspective of substance and difference from the perspective of mode are rationally supported.

Among the substance-organs (<s>dravyendriya</s>) too, with respect to each other and to the constituent <s>pudgala</s> (material) substances, <s>anekānta</s> through the doors of identity and difference

children.text: मवसेयम्, तथैव निर्बाधमुपलब्धेः । तथा च न द्रव्यमात्रं पर्यायमात्रं वेन्द्रियविषय इति
children.translated_text: should be understood, since cognition [of them] is unobstructed in that way. And thus, the object of the senses is neither substance alone nor mode alone —
touch and the rest should be seen as being instrumental in [both] action (<s>karma</s>) and [ontological] existence (<s>bhāva</s>). ‖ 21 ‖

Thus, regarding the objects of the senses such as touch and the rest, the nature of being both difference and non-difference (<s>bhedābhedātmakatva</s>), by virtue of being of the nature of both substance (<s>dravya</s>) and mode (<s>paryāya</s>),
Having said 'distinguished by substance and disposition,' [the author] now defines them in order —
The material sense organ (<s>dravyendriya</s>) consists of <s>pudgalas</s> (material aggregates) having fixed forms.

children.text: द्रव्येन्द्रियम् इत्येकवचनं जात्याश्रयणात् । नियतो विशिष्टो बाह्य आभ्य
न्तरश्चाकारः संस्थानविशेषो येषां ते नियताकाराः पूरणगलनधर्माणः स्पर्शरसगन्धवर्णव
children.translated_text: internal forms, i.e. particular configurations, possessing the properties of filling and dissolving, endowed with touch, taste, smell, and color,

children.text: न्तः पुद्गलाः, तथाहि श्रोत्रादिषु यः कर्णशष्कुलीप्रभृतिर्बाह्यः पुद्गलानां प्रचयो यश्चाभ्यन्तरः
children.translated_text: are <s>pudgalas</s> (material aggregates). For instance, in the ears and other [sense organs], the external accumulation of <s>pudgalas</s> beginning with the ear-conch,

children.text: कदम्बगोलकाद्याकारः स सर्वो द्रव्येन्द्रियम्, पुद्गलद्रव्यरूपत्वात् । अप्राधान्ये वा द्रव्य
children.translated_text: and the internal form like the <s>kadamba</s>-ball shape — all that constitutes the material sense organ (<s>dravyendriya</s>), because it is of the nature of <s>pudgala</s>-substance. Or else, the word 'substance' (<s>dravya</s>) [is used] in the sense of subordinacy,

children.text: शब्दो यथा अङ्गारमर्द्दको द्रव्याचार्य इति । अप्रधानमिन्द्रियं द्रव्येन्द्रियम्, व्यापारवत्यपि
children.translated_text: as in 'a charcoal-worker is a substance-teacher' [i.e. a minor teacher]. The subordinate sense organ is the material sense organ —even though it has activity,

children.text: तस्मिन् सन्निहितेऽपि चालोकप्रभृतिनि सहकारिपटले भावेन्द्रियं विना स्पर्शाद्यु
children.translated_text: and even when it is present together with the auxiliary apparatus such as light and the rest, without the dispositional sense organ (<s>bhāvendriya</s>), the cognition of touch and the rest
is
not established. ‖ 22 ‖
The singular 'material sense organ' (<s>dravyendriyam</s>) is because of reference to the genus (<s>jāti</s>). Those having fixed — that is, specific — external and
The dispositional sense organ (<s>bhāvendriya</s>) is attainment (<s>labdhi</s>) and cognitive activity (<s>upayoga</s>). ‖ 23 ‖
causes the <s>ātman</s> (soul) to become active

children.text: न्द्रियनिर्वृत्तिं प्रति व्याप्रियते तन्निमित्त आत्मनः परिणामविशेष उपयोगः । अत्रापि भावे
children.translated_text: toward the functioning of the material sense organ — the particular transformation of the <s>ātman</s> occasioned by that is <s>upayoga</s> (cognitive activity). Here too, the singular 'dispositional sense organ'
(<s>bhāvendriyam</s>) is because of reference to the genus. The word <s>bhāva</s> ('dispositional') has the sense of non-subordinacy.
Just as one who possesses the qualities of being <s>Indra</s>'s attendant

is called <s>Bhāvendra</s> by figurative attribution of <s>Indra</s>-ship, so too that which possesses qualities such as being an <s>Indra</s>-mark etc. by figurative attribution of such qualities is the dispositional sense organ (<s>bhāvendriya</s>).
Attainment (<s>labdhi</s>) is the obtaining [of cognitive capacity] — a particular subsidence-cum-destruction (<s>kṣayopaśama</s>) of knowledge-obscuring <s>karma</s>. That whose presence

children.text: न्द्रियतां प्रतिपद्यते । नहि तत्रायोग्यस्य तदुत्पत्तिराकाशवदुपपद्यते स्वार्थसंविद्योग्यतैव च
children.translated_text: assumes the status of a dispositional sense organ. For one who is incapable thereof cannot have its arising — like space — and the capacity for cognizing one's own objects is itself

children.text: लब्धिरिति । उपयोगस्वभावं पुनः स्वार्थसंविदि व्यापारात्मकम् । नह्यव्यापृतं स्पर्शना
children.translated_text: <s>labdhi</s> (attainment). The [sense organ] whose nature is <s>upayoga</s> (cognitive activity), however, is of the nature of active engagement in cognizing its own objects. For an inactive sensation of touch
and

children.text: संवेदनं स्पर्शादि प्रकाशयितुं शक्तम्, सुषुप्तादीनामपि तत्प्रकाशकत्वप्राप्तेः ।
children.translated_text: the like is not able to illuminate touch etc., since even deep sleep and the like would then entail such illumination.
There, the sense organ whose nature is attainment (<s>labdhi</s>), in bestowing upon the <s>ātman</s> the capacity for cognizing its own objects,

children.text: रिति चेत्; न; कारणधर्मस्य कार्येऽनुवृत्तेः । नहि पावकस्य प्रकाशकत्वे तत्कार्यस्य प्रदी
children.translated_text: no, because a property of the cause continues into the effect. For the illuminating nature of fire does not contradict the illuminating nature of the lamp, which is its effect.

children.text: पस्य प्रकाशकत्वं विरुध्यते । न च येनैव स्वभावेनोपयोगस्येन्द्रियत्वम्, तेनैव फलत्वमि
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that <s>upayoga</s> is considered to be a sense organ by the very same nature by which it is a result, such that there would be a contradiction.

children.text: ष्यते येन विरोधः स्यात् । साधकतमस्वभावेन हि तस्येन्द्रियत्वं क्रियारूपतया च फल
children.translated_text: For its nature as a sense organ is by virtue of being the most effective instrument (<s>sādhakatama</s>), and its nature as a result is by virtue of being an activity.

children.text: त्वम् । यथैव हि प्रदीपः प्रकाशात्मना प्रकाशयतीत्यत्र साधकतमः प्रकाशात्मा करणम्,
children.translated_text: Just as in the case 'a lamp illuminates by its nature of being light' — the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) having the nature of light is the most effective means, and having the nature of action it is the result,

children.text: क्रियात्मा फलम्, स्वतन्त्रत्वाच्च कर्त्तेति सर्वमिदमनेकान्तवादे न दुर्लभमित्यलं प्रसङ्गेन ॥ २३ ॥
children.translated_text: and being independent it is the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) — all this is not difficult [to maintain] in the doctrine of non-one-sidedness (<s>anekāntavāda</s>). Enough of this digression. ‖ 23 ‖

If [one objects that] when sensation, being active in illuminating its own object, has the nature of <s>upayoga</s>, then because it is a result (<s>phala</s>), its status as a sense organ (<s>indriya</s>) is untenable —
Having said 'occasioned by the mind,' [the author] now defines the mind —
The mind (<s>manas</s>) is the grasping of all objects. ‖ 24 ‖

children.text: सर्वे न तु स्पर्शनादीनां स्पर्शादिवत् प्रतिनियता एवार्था गृह्यन्तेऽनेनेति
सर्वार्थग्रहणं मनः अनिन्द्रियम् इति नोइन्द्रियम् इति चोच्यते । सर्वार्थं मन
children.translated_text: the mind, being 'the grasping of all objects,' is called 'non-sensory' (<s>anindriya</s>), i.e. 'not a sense organ' (<s>no-indriya</s>). If one says 'the mind [grasps] all objects,' there would be the undesirable extension to the <s>ātman</s> as well; hence, to convey its instrumental nature, the word 'grasping' (<s>grahaṇa</s>) is used. But the <s>ātman</s>

children.text: इत्युच्यमाने आत्मन्यपि प्रसङ्ग इति करणत्वप्रतिपादनार्थं ग्रहणम् इत्युक्तम् । आत्मा तु
children.translated_text: is the agent, so there is no over-extension. And the mind's grasping of all objects is well-established indeed. As the primary authority <s>Vācaka</s> [states],

children.text: कर्त्तेति नातिव्याप्तिः, सर्वार्थग्रहणं च मनसः प्रसिद्धमेव । यत् वाचकमुख्यः
children.translated_text: '<s>Śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge) [is the domain] of the non-sensory [mind].'
<s>Tattvārtha</s>[-sūtra] 2.22

children.text: श्रुतमिति हि विषयिणा विषयस्य निर्देशः । उपलक्षणं च
children.translated_text: '<s>Śruta</s>' — for the object is indicated by [reference to] the possessor of the object. And <s>śruta</s> is a figurative indicator

children.text: श्रुतं मतेः तेन मतिश्रुतयोर्यो विषयः स मनसो विषय इत्यर्थः ।
children.translated_text: of <s>mati</s> (sensory cognition); therefore the object of <s>mati</s> and <s>śruta</s> is the object of the mind — this is the meaning.
[extends to] substances
in not-all-modes'
'The basis of <s>mati</s> and <s>śruta</s>
<s>Tattvārtha</s>[-sūtra] 1.27
— from this statement of <s>Vācaka</s>, since <s>mati</s>-knowledge and <s>śruta</s>-knowledge have all objects [as their domain],
the mind too is established as having all objects [as its domain].
All — not like touch etc. [which are] grasped by the senses of touch etc. with fixed [respective] objects — [all] objects are grasped by this, hence

children.text: ञ्चेन्द्रियवद् द्रव्यभावभेदात् द्विविधमेव । तत्र द्रव्यमनो मनस्त्वेन
children.translated_text: is of two kinds due to the distinction between substance (<s>dravya</s>) and disposition (<s>bhāva</s>). There, the material mind (<s>dravya-manas</s>) consists of <s>pudgala</s>-substances

that have transformed into mind-ness. The dispositional mind (<s>bhāva-manas</s>), however, is the attainment (<s>labdhi</s>) consisting of the subsidence-cum-destruction of the [mind-]obscuring <s>karma</s>, and the particular activity of the <s>ātman</s>
directed toward the grasping of objects. ‖ 24 ‖
The mind too, like the five senses,

children.text: नन्वत्यल्पमिदमुच्यते इन्द्रियमनोनिमित्तः इति । अन्यदपि हि चक्षुर्ज्ञानस्य

children.translated_text: the object and light — as they say:
and the eye arises
'From form, light, mental attention,
cognition — as fire [arises] from a gem, sunlight, and cow-dung.'
To this [the author] replies —
Objection: This statement 'occasioned by the sense organs and mind' is too narrow. For there are also other causes of visual cognition —
The object and light are not the cause of knowledge, because of [their] non-exclusion [from cases where knowledge is absent]. ‖ 25 ‖

children.text: बाह्यो विषयः प्रकाशश्च न चक्षुर्ज्ञानस्य साक्षात्कारणम्, देशकालादिवत्तु व्यव

children.translated_text: is not denied — because they are accepted as remote auxiliaries within the aggregate of conditions such as the subsidence-cum-destruction of knowledge-obscuring [<s>karma</s>], like collyrium, and because the eye

children.text: रुपकारित्वेन चाभ्युपगमात् । कुतः पुनः साक्षान्न कारणत्वमित्याह--अव्यतिरेकात्
children.translated_text: [is accepted] as a helper. Why then are they not direct causes? — [the author] says: 'because of non-exclusion' (<s>avyatirekāt</s>),

children.text: व्यतिरेकाभावात् । न हि तद्भावे भावलक्षणोऽन्वय एव हेतुफलभावनिश्चयनिमित्तम्,
children.translated_text: i.e. because of the absence of exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>). For it is not only co-presence (<s>anvaya</s>) — the characteristic of being present when [the effect] is present — that determines the cause-effect relationship,

children.text: अपि तु तदभावेऽभावलक्षणो व्यतिरेकोऽपि । न चासावर्थालोकयोर्हेतुभावेऽस्ति; मरु

Having concluded inference-for-others, he now defines refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>), which is its natural accompaniment —
The exposing of a defect in the proof (<s>sādhana</s>) is refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>). ॥ 28 ॥

children.translated_text: the exposing of these, i.e., that by which they are brought to light, i.e., the statement that exposes the defects of the proof, is refutation. Since the word 'bhūta' (actual) is used in the definition,
it is established that only the exposing of actual
defects constitutes refutation. ॥ 28 ॥
The defects of the proof — i.e., of inference-for-others — such as the unestablished, the contradictory, etc., that were stated earlier —

The exposings of non-existent defects are pseudo-refutations (<s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s>), [which are also called] <s>jātyuttara</s> (sophistical rejoinders). ॥ 29 ॥

children.text: सादृश्येनोत्तराणि जात्युत्तराणि । तानि च सम्यग्घेतौ हेत्वाभासे वा वादिना प्रयुक्ते झटिति
children.translated_text: Replies [made] through similarity are <s>jāti</s>-replies (futile rejoinders). These, when a valid reason or a pseudo-reason is employed by the debater, and the fault or truth of it does not immediately appear,
being mostly reflections of the reason, the counter-positions are infinite in number and cannot be enumerated.
Nevertheless, following the direction shown by <s>Akṣapāda</s> (Gautama), through the classification of counter-positions based on similarity and the like, [they are shown as:]

<s>sādharmya</s> (similarity), <s>vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity), <s>utkarṣa</s> (elevation), <s>apakarṣa</s> (degradation), <s>varṇya</s> (describable), <s>avarṇya</s> (indescribable), <s>vikalpa</s> (alternative), <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>aprāpti</s> (non-attainment), <s>prasaṅga</s> (implication), <s>pratidṛṣṭānta</s> (counter-example), <s>anutpatti</s> (non-origination), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (topic), <s>ahetu</s> (non-reason),

<s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>aviśeṣa</s> (non-distinction), <s>upapatti</s> (cogency), <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension), <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), <s>nitya</s> (eternal), <s>anitya</s> (non-eternal), and <s>kārya</s> (effect)
— twenty-four are demonstrated in the form of equalities (<s>sama</s>).

In the very same argument 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced,

is only in the mode of

children.text: अविशेषापादनेन प्रत्यवस्थानमविशेषसमा जातिः । यथा यदि शब्दघटयोरेको धर्मः
children.translated_text: Counter-position through establishing non-distinction is the <s>aviśeṣasamā jāti</s>. For example: 'If one property — being-produced — is accepted as common to sound and the pot,

children.translated_text: being-produced, why should it not also be permanent through the cogency of being partless?' The intended [conclusion] is that, since both sides have

children.translated_text: is made, the counter-position is: 'Surely being immediately preceded by effort is not a proof for impermanence. For a proof

children.text: तदुच्यते येन विना न साध्यमुपलभ्यते । उपलभ्यते च प्रयत्नानन्तरीयकत्वेन विनाऽपि
children.translated_text: is that without which the probandum is not apprehended. But impermanence is apprehended even without being immediately preceded by effort,
as in lightning and the like. And in sound too, sometimes in [sounds] produced by plants broken by the force of wind, and the like.' (20)

children.text: अनुपलब्ध्या प्रत्यवस्थानमनुपलब्धिसमा जातिः । यथा तत्रैव प्रयत्नानन्तरीयक
children.translated_text: Counter-position through non-apprehension is the <s>anupalabdhisamā jāti</s>. For example, when the very same reason of being immediately preceded by effort

children.translated_text: is presented, the <s>jāti</s>-debater says: 'Sound is not an effect of effort. Before utterance, it already
exists, but due to

children.text: रणयोगात्तु नोपलभ्यते । आवरणानुपलम्भेऽप्यनुपलम्भान्नास्त्येव शब्द इति चेत्
children.translated_text: being obstructed (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), it is not apprehended. And if [one argues] that from the non-apprehension of the obstruction too, through non-apprehension, sound simply does not exist;'
no,
because non-apprehension exists even when the obstruction is not apprehended. And from the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of obstruction, [follows its] absence; and in its absence,
there is the presence of the apprehension of obstruction. Therefore, just as a root-peg or water covered by clay [exists though hidden], the non-grasping of sound

children.text: प्रयत्नेन शब्दो विवक्षितो जन्यत एव न तु व्यज्यते ।

children.translated_text: (21) The <s>nityasamā</s>

children.text: धर्मनित्यानित्यत्वविकल्पेन शब्दनित्यत्वापादनं नित्यसमा जातिः । यथा अनित्यः शब्द
children.translated_text: <s>jāti</s> is establishing the permanence of sound through the alternative of the probandum-property being permanent or impermanent. For example, when 'Sound is impermanent'

children.text: इति प्रतिज्ञाते जातिवादी विकल्पयति--येयमनित्यता शब्दस्योच्यते सा किमनित्या
children.translated_text: is asserted, the <s>jāti</s>-debater presents the alternative: 'This impermanence that is predicated of sound — is it impermanent

children.translated_text: or permanent?' If impermanent, then it will necessarily pass away; and from the passing away of impermanence, sound is permanent.
If impermanence is permanent

children.text: व; तथापि धर्मस्य नित्यत्वात्तस्य च निराश्रयस्यानुपपत्तेस्तदाश्रय

is permanent.
(22) Counter-position through establishing the impermanence of all entities is the <s>anityasamā jāti</s>. For example:

children.text: साधर्म्यमनित्येन शब्दस्यास्तीति तस्यानित्यत्वं यदि प्रतिपाद्यते, तद् घटेन सर्वपदार्था
children.translated_text: 'If the impermanence of sound is established from similarity with the pot, which is impermanent, then all entities

(23) Counter-position through presenting the diversity of effects of effort is the <s>kāryasamā jāti</s>.

children.text: कार्यसमा जातिः । यथा अनित्यः शब्दः प्रयत्नानन्तरीयकत्वादित्युक्ते जातिवाद्याह-
children.translated_text: For example, when it is said 'Sound is impermanent, because of being immediately preceded by effort,' the <s>jāti</s>-debater says:

children.translated_text: 'A twofold nature of effort is observed: some things are produced by it that did not exist before, like a pot; while some things that already exist are merely manifested
