children.translated_text: whether sound is manifested or produced by effort.' Since the mode of establishing doubt differs, the <s>kāryasamā</s>
<s>jāti</s> is distinct from the <s>saṃśayasamā</s>. (24)

Of these, counter-position through similarity is the <s>sādharmyasamā jāti</s> (similarity-equality futile rejoinder). For example, when the argument 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>),

children.text: क्षया चतुर्विंशतिर्जातिभेदा एते दर्शिताः । प्रतिसमाधानं तु सर्वजातीनामन्यथानुप
children.translated_text: have been shown here with distinct, unmixed examples. The counter-remedy for all <s>jātis</s>, however, is simply the examination of
the criterion of inference, characterized by <s>anyathānupapatti</s> (otherwise-inexplicability).
For against a reason whose criteria are unimpaired, such dust-throwing objections have no force.
And since the connection of being-produced and being-immediately-preceded-by-effort [with impermanence] is firm, the non-apprehension of sound

children.text: म्भनमपि त्वनित्यत्वकृतमेव । जातिप्रयोगे च परेण कृते सम्यगुत्तरमेव वक्तव्यं न
children.translated_text: is not due to obstruction but is indeed due to [its] impermanence. When the opponent employs a <s>jāti</s>-argument, one should give only a proper reply, not
counter with further <s>jāti</s>-replies in return, lest the proceedings become absurd.
Thus, although the <s>jātis</s> are infinite through differences in the mode of raising objections and in alternative objects, twenty-four types of <s>jāti</s>
For it has been said that through differences in the mode of

children.text: भेदेनानन्तानि जात्युत्तराणीति । तत्र परस्य वदतोऽर्थविकल्पोपपादनेन वचनविघात
children.translated_text: raising objections, <s>jāti</s>-replies are infinite. Of these, the undermining of an opponent's statement by establishing an alternative meaning of his words is <s>chala</s> (quibble).

children.text: श्छलम् । तत्त्रिधा वाक्छलं सामान्यच्छलमुपचारच्छलं चेति । तत्र साधारणे शब्दे प्रयुक्ते
children.translated_text: It is of three kinds: <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibble), <s>sāmānyachala</s> (generality quibble), and <s>upacārachala</s> (figurative quibble). Of these, when a common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) word is used,
construing a meaning other than what the speaker

children.text: दर्थादर्थान्तरकल्पनया तन्निषेधो वाक्छलम् । यथा नवकम्बलोऽयं माण
children.translated_text: intended and negating [the statement] is <s>vākchala</s>. For example, when someone says 'This boy is <s>navakambala</s>' meaning 'having a new blanket,'

children.text: वक इति नूतनविवक्षया कथिते परः सङ्ख्यामारोप्य निषेधति--कुतोऽस्य नव कम्बला
children.translated_text: the other, imposing the numerical meaning, refutes: 'How does he have nine blankets?'

children.text: इति ? । सम्भावनयातिप्रसङ्गिनोऽपि सामान्यस्योपन्यासे हेतुत्वारोपणेन तन्निषेधः सामा
children.translated_text: Attributing the status of a reason to a general property that leads to over-extension, through [mere] probability, and negating it is <s>sāmānyachala</s>

children.text: न्यच्छलम् । यथा अहो नु खल्वसौ ब्राह्मणो विद्याचरणसम्पन्न इति ब्राह्मणस्तुतिप्रसङ्गे
children.translated_text: (generality quibble). For example, when someone in the context of praising a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> says 'Ah, this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is endowed with learning and conduct,'

children.text: कश्चिद्वदति--सम्भवति ब्राह्मणे विद्याचरणसम्पदिति । तत् छलवादी ब्राह्मणत्वस्य हेतुता
children.translated_text: someone says: 'It is possible that a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has learning and conduct.' Then the quibbler, attributing causal status

children.text: मारोप्य निराकुर्वन्नभियुङ्क्ते--यदि ब्राह्मणे विद्याचरणसम्पद् भवति, व्रात्येऽपि सा भवेत्
children.translated_text: to <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood, refutes: 'If learning and conduct exist in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, then they should exist in a <s>vrātya</s> (degraded brāhmaṇa) too,

children.text: व्रात्योऽपि ब्राह्मण एवेति । औपचारिके प्रयोगे मुख्यप्रतिषेधेन प्रत्यवस्थानमुपचार
children.translated_text: since a <s>vrātya</s> is also a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' Counter-positioning a figurative usage by negating its literal meaning is <s>upacārachala</s>

children.text: च्छलम् । यथा मञ्चाः क्रोशन्तीति उक्ते परः प्रत्यवतिष्ठते--कथमचेतनाः मञ्चाः क्रोशन्ति
children.translated_text: (figurative quibble). For example, when someone says 'The platforms are crying,' the other objects: 'How can inanimate platforms cry?

children.text: मञ्चस्थास्तु पुरुषाः क्रोशन्तीति । तदत्र छलत्रयेऽपि वृद्धव्यवहारप्रसिद्धशब्दसामर्थ्य
children.translated_text: It is the people on the platforms who are crying.' Here, in all three types of <s>chala</s>, the proper remedy
should be understood as simply examining the capacity of words as established in the usage of the wise. (29)
<s>Chala</s> (quibble) too, since it lacks the character of a proper reply, is itself a type of <s>jāti</s>-reply.

children.text: साधनदूषणाद्यभिधानं च प्रायो वादे भवतीति वादस्य लक्षणमाह--
children.translated_text: Since the declaration of proof and refutation generally occurs in debate (<s>vāda</s>), he states the definition of <s>vāda</s>:
for the purpose of protecting truth. (30)
<s>Vāda</s> (debate) is the statement of proof and refutation in the presence of judges (<s>prāśnika</s>) and others,

children.text: स्वपक्षसिद्धये वादिनः साधनम् तत्प्रतिषेधाय प्रतिवादिनो दूषणम् ।
प्रतिवादिनोऽपि स्वपक्षसिद्धये साधनम् तत्प्रतिषेधाय वादिनो दूषणम् । तदेवं वादिनः
children.translated_text: For establishing his own thesis too, the respondent offers proof; for negating it, the proponent offers refutation. Thus, the proponent's
proof and refutation of the opponent's proof and refuta-
tion — the speaking, i.e. the stating, by both the proponent and the opponent,
is <s>vāda</s> (debate). How? — [The author] says: 'in the presence of assessors (<s>prāśnika</s>) and others.' The assessors are the jurors —
'Knowledgeable in their own and others' doctrines, of noble birth, desired by both parties, patient,
skilled in the paths of debate, impartial like a balance — these are called <s>prāśnikas</s> (assessors).'

children.text: त्येवंलक्षणाः । आदिग्रहणेन सभापतिवादिप्रतिवादिपरिग्रहः, सेयं चतुरङ्गा कथा,
children.translated_text: Such are their characteristics. By the word 'and others' (<s>ādi</s>), the president of the assembly (<s>sabhāpati</s>), the proponent, and the opponent are included. This is a four-limbed debate (<s>kathā</s>),

children.text: एकस्याप्यङ्गस्य वैकल्ये कथात्वानुपपत्तेः । नहि वर्णाश्रमपालनक्षमं न्यायान्यायव्य
children.translated_text: since in the absence of even one limb, the status of [proper] debate is not established. For without an assembly-president who is capable of upholding <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s> [duties], who establishes what is logical and what is not,

children.text: वस्थापकं पक्षपातरहितत्वेन समदृष्टिं सभापतिं यथोक्तलक्षणांश्च प्राश्निकान् विना
children.translated_text: who has equal vision by being free from partiality, and without assessors having the stated characteristics,

children.translated_text: Since we observe that even one who, having asserted something as the <s>sādhya</s>, then asserts its opposite — [due to] human
error having multiple
causes. (1)
Among these, the definition of abandoning the thesis (<s>pratijñāhāni</s>) —

धतः प्रतिज्ञान्तरं नाम निग्रहस्थानं भवति । अनित्यः शब्दः ऐन्द्रियकत्वादित्युक्ते

children.translated_text: 'Sound is not omnipresent,' is defeated by [the charge of] shifting the thesis. This too, like abandoning the thesis, is

causes.

children.translated_text: And how does this differ from abandoning the thesis, since the relinquishment of the <s>pakṣa</s> is the same

children.text: त्राविशेषात् ? । यथैव हि प्रतिदृष्टान्तधर्मस्य स्वदृष्टान्तेऽभ्यनुज्ञानात् पक्षत्यागस्तथा प्रति
children.translated_text: in both cases? For just as thesis-abandonment [occurs] through acknowledging the property of the counter-example in one's own example, so too [it occurs] through shifting the thesis.

children.text: ज्ञान्तरादपि । यथा च स्वपक्षसिद्ध्यर्थं प्रतिज्ञान्तरं विधीयते तथा शब्दानित्यत्वसि
children.translated_text: And just as the shifting of the thesis is done for the purpose of establishing one's own thesis, so too the acknowledgment
'Let sound too be permanent' out of confusion [is done] for the purpose of establishing the impermanence of sound;

children.text: शात् तद्वच्छब्दोऽपि नित्योऽस्तु इत्यनुज्ञानम्, यथा चाभ्रान्तस्येदं विरुद्ध्यते
children.translated_text: and just as this [latter] is contradictory for one who is not confused,
so too is the shifting of the thesis. And if they are differentiated by difference of cause, the consequence would be that further undesired defeat-points too

children.text: तेषां च तत्रान्तर्भावे प्रतिज्ञान्तरस्यापि प्रतिज्ञाहानावन्तर्भावः स्यादिति २ ।
children.translated_text: And if they are subsumed therein, then shifting the thesis too should be subsumed under abandoning the thesis. (2)
When the opponent has negated the asserted proposition, if [the proponent] states a different property of the very same property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) as what is to be proved,
'The contradiction between the thesis and the reason is contradicting the thesis (<s>pratijñāvirodha</s>).'
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.4
— this is a defeat-

children.text: स्थानं भवति । यथा गुणव्यतिरिक्तं द्रव्यं रूपादिभ्योऽर्थान्तरस्यानुपलब्धेरिति । सोऽयं
children.translated_text: point. For example: 'Substance is different from qualities, because of the non-perception of something different from color and the like.' This is
the contradiction between thesis and reason: if substance is different from qualities, how can there be non-perception of something different from color etc.?

children.text: अथ रूपादिभ्योऽर्थान्तरस्यानुपलब्धिः कथं गुणव्यतिरिक्तं द्रव्यमिति ?, तदयं प्रतिज्ञा
children.translated_text: And if there is non-perception of something different from color etc., how can substance be different from qualities? This [debater],

children.text: विरुद्धाभिधानात् पराजीयते । तदेतदसङ्गतम् । यतो हेतुना प्रतिज्ञायाः प्रतिज्ञात्वे निरस्ते
children.translated_text: having stated something contradictory to his thesis, is defeated. But this is incongruous, because when the thesis-status of the thesis is negated by the reason,

children.translated_text: this is simply a form of abandoning the thesis from a different perspective, or it is a defect of the reason — namely, the contradictory [reason] — not a defect of the
thesis. (3)

children.text: पक्षसाधने परेण दूषिते तदुद्धरणाशक्त्या प्रतिज्ञामेव निह्नुवानस्य प्रति
ज्ञासंन्यासो नाम निग्रहस्थानं भवति । यथा अनित्यः शब्दः ऐन्द्रियकत्वादित्युक्ते
children.translated_text: there arises the defeat-point called 'renouncing the thesis' (<s>pratijñāsaṃnyāsa</s>). For example, when it is stated 'Sound is impermanent because of being perceptible,'

children.translated_text: and inconclusiveness has been pointed out through the universal, if one were to say — 'Who says that sound is impermanent?' —

children.text: ति--स प्रतिज्ञासंन्यासात् पराजितो भवतीति । एतदपि प्रतिज्ञाहानितो न भिद्यते,
children.translated_text: — he is defeated by abandoning his thesis. This too does not differ from 'abandonment of the thesis' (<s>pratijñāhāni</s>),
since here too there is no difference in the abandonment of the thesis through apprehending the inconclusiveness of the reason. [4]
When the opponent has refuted the proof of the thesis, [the proponent], unable to rebut [the refutation], denying his very thesis — for this person

children.text: अविशेषाभिहिते हेतौ प्रतिषिद्धे तद्विशेषणमभिदधतो हेत्वन्तरं नाम
निग्रहस्थानं भवति । तस्मिन्नेव प्रयोगे तथैव सामान्य
children.translated_text: a ground of defeat. In the very same formulation, when the general [reason] is refuted by showing deviation —
[the proponent] adducing a qualifier such as 'given that it possesses a universal'
and
the like — is defeated by [the charge of] resorting to another reason. This too is over-extended,

children.translated_text: since when a generally stated example, application, or conclusion is refuted, one who wishes to add a qualifier would also be subject to [the charge of] resorting to another example, etc.,
as a different ground of defeat, for in those cases too the objection and response are of the same kind. [5]
When a reason that has been stated in general terms is refuted, and [the proponent] then adduces a qualifier [to that reason], this is called 'resorting to another reason' (<s>hetvantara</s>),
(<s>anaupaiyika</s>), different from the subject under discussion, this is called 'irrelevance' (<s>arthāntara</s>), a ground

children.translated_text: of defeat. For example: 'Sound is impermanent. [Why?] Because of being produced — this is the reason.' 'The word "reason" (<s>hetu</s>) is a <s>kṛdanta</s> (primary derivative) formed with the <s>tu</s>-suffix from the root <s>hi</s> (to impel).'
'A word (<s>pada</s>) [is one of four types:]
noun, verb, particle, and prefix' — launching into

children.translated_text: is defeated by [the charge of] irrelevance. This ground of defeat called 'irrelevance' — does it serve as a ground of defeat when a competent proof or refutation has been offered,

And when incompetent — would it be a ground of defeat when the opponent's thesis is established, or when it is not?
In the first case, [the proponent's] defeat is due to the establishment of the opponent's thesis
itself, not from this
ground of defeat. In the second case too, there is no defeat from this,
since in neither case has the thesis been established. [6]
When one states something irrelevant

children.translated_text: every ground of defeat would be [reducible to] 'meaninglessness,' since there is no difference in being useless for establishing the thesis. [And if one says there is defeat] from some slight
distinction alone,
then even clapping hands, slapping one's armpit, and the like, being useless for the thesis, would become additional
grounds of defeat. [7]
The mere utterance of a sequence of syllables devoid of denotation is called 'meaninglessness' (<s>nirarthaka</s>), a ground of defeat.

children.text: यत् साधनवाक्यं दूषणवाक्यं वा त्रिरभिहितमपि परिषत्प्रतिवादिभ्यां बोद्धुं

children.translated_text: a ground of defeat. Here we say: a statement uttered three times by the proponent but not understood by the assembly and the opponent — [is this] because of their
dull-wittedness, because of obscure
expression, or because of rapid
utterance? In the first case, this ground of defeat would apply even to a proponent with a valid proof, since even then
it is possible that these two [i.e., the assembly and the opponent], being dull-witted,
fail to understand. In the second case, [the charge] would apply even when a written statement is used,
since even an obscure
expression
may not be understood even by very intelligent members of the assembly and the opponent. But if these two fail to understand, the proponent
explains [it]; let him explain even his own obscure presentation;

children.text: मप्यात्मनः स एव व्याचष्टाम्, अव्याख्याने तु जयाभाव एवास्य,
children.translated_text: if he does not explain, then he merely fails to win,

children.text: न पुनर्निग्रहः, परस्य पक्षसिद्धेरभावात् । द्रुतोच्चारेप्यनयोः कथञ्चित् ज्ञानं सम्भवत्येव,
children.translated_text: but is not defeated, since the opponent's thesis is not established. In the case of rapid utterance too, these two can somehow understand,
since
they know both doctrinal systems. But when the proponent's mere babbling

children.text: एवं ब्रूयात् वादिनः प्रलापमात्रम् अविज्ञातस्य लक्षणम् इत्याशङ्कायामाह

children.translated_text: is useless for the thesis,
their failure to understand
is not [a case of]

children.translated_text: 'unintelligible meaning' — like the mere statement of a sequence of phonemes. Therefore this 'unintelligible meaning' does not differ from 'meaninglessness.' [8]
When a statement of proof or refutation, even after being uttered three times, cannot be understood by the assembly and the opponent, this is called 'unintelligible meaning' (<s>avijñātārtha</s>),

children.text: भवति । यथा दश दाडिमानि षडपूपा इत्यादि । एतदपि निरर्थकान्न भिद्यते । यथैव
children.translated_text: a ground of defeat. For example: 'ten pomegranates, six cakes,' and so forth. This too does not differ from 'meaninglessness.' For just as
there is meaninglessness of the phonemes in <s>ga-ja-ḍa-da-ba</s> and the like, so here

children.text: त्र पदानामिति । यदि पुनः पदनैरर्थक्यं वर्ण
children.translated_text: there is meaninglessness of the words. Now, if the meaninglessness of words, being different from the meaninglessness of phonemes,
constitutes a separate ground of defeat — then the meaninglessness of sentences, being different from both of those,
would also be a separate
ground of defeat; for sentences too, like words, can be found in many ways that are not properly sequenced —

children.text: शङ्खः कदल्यां कदली च भेर्यां तस्यां च भेर्यां सुमहद्विमानम् ।
children.translated_text: 'A conch in a plantain, and a plantain in a drum, and in that drum a great aerial chariot;
that conch-drum-plantain-chariot became like the mad <s>Gaṅgā</s>.'
— And so forth.
The use of a collection of words whose earlier and later parts are unconnected, resulting in an unestablished sentence-meaning, is called 'incoherence' (<s>apārthaka</s>),

children.text: दश दाडिमानि षडपूपा इत्यत्र तु पदानामेव नैरर्थक्यम् न वाक्यस्य क्रियाया अश्रावणत्वात्

children.translated_text: is itself the meaninglessness of sentences, since [sentences] consist of collections of words,

children.text: तर्हि वर्णनैरर्थक्यमेव पदनैरर्थक्यं स्यात् वर्णसमुदायात्मकत्वात् तस्य । वर्णानां सर्वत्र निर
children.translated_text: then the meaninglessness of phonemes would itself be the meaninglessness of words, since [words] consist of collections of phonemes. [Objection:] Since phonemes are always

children.translated_text: meaningless, the same would follow for words too. [Response:] Then, since words are meaningless, the same would follow for sentences,
which consist of collections of words. [Objection:] But words are meaningful because they depend on
word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>).
[Response:] By dependence on phoneme-meaning,
phon-
emes too would be [meaningful].

children.text: स्तु प्रकृतिप्रत्ययादिवत्; न खलु प्रकृतिः केवला पदं प्रत्ययो वा । नाप्यन
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But [phonemes function] like a root (<s>prakṛti</s>) and a suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>); for neither a root alone nor a suffix alone constitutes a word, and yet neither of the
two

children.text: नर्थकत्वम् । अभिव्यक्तार्थाभावादनर्थकत्वे; पदस्यापि तत् स्यात् । यथैव हि प्रकृत्यर्थः
children.translated_text: is meaningless. [Response:] If [phonemes are] meaningless because of the absence of a manifested meaning, then the same would apply to words too. For just as the meaning of the root

children.text: प्रत्ययेनाभिव्यज्यते प्रत्ययार्थश्च प्रकृत्या तयोः केवलयोरप्रयोगात् तथा देवदत्तस्तिष्ठती
children.translated_text: is manifested by the suffix and the meaning of the suffix by the root — since neither is used alone — so too in the expression '<s>Devadatta</s> stands' (<s>Devadattastiṣṭhati</s>),
the meaning of the first word ending in <s>sya</s> is manifested by the latter word ending in <s>ti</s>,
and [vice versa] — the independent [word] is not used [alone].

children.text: प्रयोगः । पदान्तरापेक्षस्य पदस्य सार्थकत्वं प्रकृत्यपेक्षस्य प्रत्ययस्य तदपेक्षस्य
children.translated_text: The meaningfulness of a word that depends on another word is the same as that of a suffix that depends on a root, and of a root-phoneme, etc.,
that depends on [its context]. [9]
But if the meaninglessness of words

children.text: मानमनुमानवाक्यमप्राप्तकालं नाम निग्रहस्थानं भवति, स्वप्रतिपत्तिवत् परप्रतिपत्तेर्जनने
children.translated_text: this is called 'untimely' (<s>aprāptakāla</s>), a ground of defeat — since in inference-for-others, the order too is a component for generating the other's understanding, just as in one's own understanding.
This too is ill-considered, since it is observed that intelligent listeners understand the meaning even without a fixed order of the members.
Objection: Just as from a corrupt word (<s>apaśabda</s>), one recalls
the [correct] word and thence understands the meaning —

children.text: शब्दादेवार्थप्रत्ययः परम्परया तथा प्रतिज्ञाद्यवयवव्युत्क्रमात् तत्क्रमस्मरणं ततो वाक्या
children.translated_text: so that the understanding of meaning from a [corrupt] word is indirect — similarly, from the disorder of the members like thesis, etc., one recalls their [correct] order, and thence understands the sentence-meaning,

children.text: र्थप्रत्ययो न पुनस्तद्व्युत्क्रमात्; इत्यप्यसारम्, एवंविधप्रतीत्यभावात् । यस्माद्धि शब्दा
children.translated_text: not directly from their disorder. — This too is unsound, since such a [two-step] cognition does not occur. For the very [word-form] from which, when uttered, there is a cognition of a particular meaning — that alone is its designator, not another;

children.text: दुच्चरितात् यत्रार्थे प्रतीतिः स एव तस्य वाचको नान्यः, अन्यथा शब्दात्तत्क्रमाच्चापशब्दे

explanation is observed even in corrupt words.
And if [you accept] the rule that from a correct (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) word arises merit (<s>dharma</s>) and from
another [i.e., corrupt word] demerit (<s>adharma</s>), then the practice of means to merit and demerit other [than correct speech] would be pointless,
and the non-fixation of merit and demerit would follow, since
[correct] words are observed in both unrighteous and righteous

children.translated_text: [speakers]. Or, even granting that the understanding of meaning [arises] from the [correct] order, still, the statement that scrambles the order by which the meaning was understood in its proper sequence

children.text: मवचनानुषङ्गात् । अथ सामर्थ्याद्गम्यमानस्यापि यत् सत् तत् सर्वं
children.translated_text: the subsumption itself. If it be said that, although something is understood by implication, the statement of the subsumption—'Whatever exists is

children.text: क्षणिकं यथा घटः, संश्च शब्द इति पक्षधर्मोपसंहारस्य व
children.translated_text: momentary, like a pot, and sound too exists'—is for the purpose of excluding the non-establishment of the reason as a property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>);
then why should not the statement of the reason, in spite of being
a non-property of the subject,

be for the purpose of excluding unestablishment? Then, for removing doubt about the locus of the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved), the statement of the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) too, even though understood,

and the statement of the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) for showing the unity of purpose of the thesis, reason, example, and application (<s>pratijñā</s>, <s>hetu</s>, <s>udāharaṇa</s>, <s>upanaya</s>)—
why should they not be made? For without showing the unity of purpose of the thesis etc.,

children.text: न स्यात् ? । नहि प्रतिज्ञादीनामेकार्थत्वोपदर्शनमन्तरेण सङ्गतत्वं घटते, भिन्नविषय
children.translated_text: coherence is not established, just as in the case of a thesis etc. with different subjects. But if the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved) is established from the thesis alone, the statement of the reason etc. would be

children.text: प्रतिज्ञादिवत् । ननु प्रतिज्ञातः साध्यसिद्धौ हेत्वादिवचनमनर्थकमेव स्यात्, अन्यथा
children.translated_text: pointless, otherwise it would not be a component of proof—if this is objected; then for you too, if the <s>sādhya</s> is established from the reason, the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) would be

children.text: नास्याः साधनाङ्गतेति चेत्; तर्हि भवतोऽपि हेतुतः साध्यसिद्धौ दृष्टान्तोऽनर्थकः
children.translated_text: pointless, otherwise it would not be a component of proof—the same [objection applies]. But the example is not pointless because it serves to show the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) between the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof),

children.text: स्यात्, अन्यथा नास्य साधनाङ्गतेति समानम् । ननु साध्यसाधनयोर्व्याप्तिप्रदर्शनार्थ
children.translated_text: and without showing that therein, the reason would be non-probative—this too is incorrect, since in proving the universal impermanence [of all things],

children.text: त्वात् नानर्थको दृष्टान्तः, तत्र तदप्रदर्शने हेतोरगमकत्वात्; इत्यप्ययुक्तम्, सर्वानित्यत्व
children.translated_text: because an example is impossible for <s>sattva</s> (existence) etc., the consequence of non-probativeness would follow. If the probativeness of <s>sattva</s> etc. is [established] through exclusion from the counter-instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>),

children.text: वा सर्वत्रापि हेतौ तथैव गमकत्वप्रसङ्गात् दृष्टान्तोऽनर्थक एव स्यात् । विपक्षव्यावृत्त्या
children.translated_text: then in every case the reason too would be probative in the same way, so the example would be utterly pointless. And how could one who supports the reason through exclusion from the counter-instance

children.text: च हेतुं समर्थयन् कथं प्रतिज्ञां प्रतिक्षिपेत् ? । तस्याश्चानभिधाने क्व हेतुः साध्यं वा
children.translated_text: reject the thesis? And without stating it, where would the reason or the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved)

children.text: वर्तते ? । गम्यमाने प्रतिज्ञाविषय एवेति चेत्; तर्हि गम्यमानस्यैव हेतोरपि समर्थनं
children.translated_text: operate? If it be said that [they operate] in the subject matter of the thesis which is understood [implicitly]; then the support too would be of the reason that is merely understood,

children.text: स्यान्न तूक्तस्य । अथ गम्यमानस्यापि हेतोर्मन्दमतिप्रतिपत्त्यर्थं वचनम्; तथा प्रतिज्ञा
children.translated_text: not of the one [explicitly] stated. If the statement of even an understood reason is for the comprehension of the dull-witted; then what dissatisfaction could there be with the statement of the
thesis?

And the interpretation of this [term 'not a component of proof']—<s>sādhana</s> (proof) means establishment, its component (<s>aṅga</s>) is the triple-characterized mark (<s>trirūpaliṅga</s>), and its non-statement—

children.text: वचनम्, वैधर्म्येण च प्रयोगे साधर्म्यवचनं गम्यमानत्वात् पुनरुक्तमतो न साधनाङ्गम्;
children.translated_text: and when stated by negative concomitance, the statement by positive concomitance, being already understood, is redundant and hence not a component of proof—

children.text: इत्यप्यसाम्प्रतम्, यतः सम्यक्साधनसामर्थ्येन स्वपक्षं साधयतो वादिनो निग्रहः
children.translated_text: this too is improper, because does the proponent who establishes his own position through the power of correct proof incur defeat,
or does the one who does not establish it? In the first case, defeat does not come merely from the charge of excess statement that does not obstruct the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s>,

children.text: णास्य निग्रहः, अविरोधात् । नन्वेवं नाटकादिघोषणतोऽप्यस्य निग्रहो न स्यात्; सत्य
children.translated_text: since there is no contradiction. But then, defeat should not follow even from announcing a dance performance etc.; true,

children.text: मेतत्, स्वसाध्यं प्रसाध्य नृत्यतोऽपि दोषाभावाल्लोकवत्, अन्यथा ताम्बूलभक्षण
children.translated_text: since there is no fault even in dancing after having established one's <s>sādhya</s>, just as in worldly affairs; otherwise, defeat would follow even for a proponent with a valid proof, from chewing betel,
raising eyebrows, clearing the throat, clapping hands, and so on. But if

children.text: स्वपक्षमप्रसाधयतोऽस्य ततो निग्रहः; नन्वत्रापि किं प्रतिवादिना स्वपक्षे साधिते
children.translated_text: defeat occurs for one who has not established his own position; then here too, is the charge of excess statement when the respondent has established his own position considered as defeat for the proponent, or when he has not? In the first case,

children.text: वादिनो वचनाधिक्योपालम्भो निग्रहो लक्ष्येत, असाधिते वा ? । प्रथमपक्षे स्वपक्षसिद्ध्यै
children.translated_text: since the proponent's defeat is by the very establishment of [the respondent's] own position, raising the charge of excess statement is pointless, since even with that [charge],

children.text: वास्य निग्रहाद्वचनाधिक्योद्भावनमनर्थकम्, तस्मिन् सत्यपि पक्षसिद्धिमन्तरेण जया
children.translated_text: victory is not possible without the establishment of the thesis.

children.text: योगात् । द्वितीयपक्षे तु युगपद्वादिप्रतिवादिनोः पराजयप्रसङ्गो जयप्रसङ्गो वा स्यात्,
children.translated_text: In the second case, there would be the consequence of simultaneous defeat or simultaneous victory of both proponent and respondent,
since there is no difference in the non-establishment of their respective positions.
And the alternative interpretation of 'not a component of proof'—when the reason is stated by positive concomitance (<s>sādharmya</s>), the statement by negative concomitance (<s>vaidharmya</s>),

children.text: त्वात् । साधनवादिना हि साधुसाधनं ज्ञात्वा वक्तव्यम्, दूषणवादिना च दूषणम् । तत्र
children.translated_text: for the proponent of proof must state the proof knowing it to be correct, and the proponent of refutation must [know] the refutation. In that case,
when the meaning is understood either from the statement by positive concomitance (<s>sādharmya</s>) or from the statement by negative concomitance

children.text: धर्म्यवचनाद्वैधर्म्यवचनाद्वाऽर्थस्य प्रतिपत्तौ तदुभयवचने वादिनः प्रतिवादिना सभा
children.translated_text: (<s>vaidharmya</s>), if the proponent states both, the respondent in the assembly raises the charge of stating what is not a component of proof, thereby establishing the proponent's ignorance of correct proof, leading to defeat.
And the respondent would have victory due to the determination of knowledge of refutation—

children.text: षणज्ञाननिर्णयाज्जयः स्यात्; इत्यप्यविचारितरमणीयम्, यतः स प्रतिवादी सत्साधन
children.translated_text: this too is attractive only when not examined carefully, because would that respondent raise the fault of excess statement against a proponent with valid proof

children.text: वादिनः साधनाभासवादिनो वा वचनाधिक्यदोषमुद्भावयेत् ? । तत्राद्यपक्षे वादिनः कथं
children.translated_text: or against a proponent with fallacious proof? In the first case, how can the proponent be ignorant of correct proof,

children.text: साधुसाधनाज्ञानम्, तद्वचनेयत्ताज्ञानस्यैवाभावात् ? । द्वितीयपक्षे तु न प्रतिवादिनो
children.translated_text: since there is no ignorance of the extent of its statement? In the second case, the respondent's knowledge of refutation does not hold,
since the fallacious proof has not been exposed. If it be said that
from knowledge of the fault of excess statement, he is one who knows refutation;
[we reply:] from ignorance of the fallacious proof, he is also one who does not know refutation, so he cannot conclusively
defeat the proponent, since the defeat characterized by failure to expose that [fallacious proof]
cannot be prevented either. If the respondent's victory is established merely by raising the charge of excess statement,
then exposing the fallacious proof would be pointless; but then, if the respondent's defeat is established by not exposing the fallacious proof,

children.text: त्तस्य पराजयसिद्धौ वचनाधिक्योद्भावनं कथं जयाय प्रकल्पेत ? । अथ वचनाधिक्यं
children.translated_text: how could the raising of [the charge of] excess statement serve as grounds for victory? If the respondent achieves victory by raising either the [charge of] excess statement
or the fallacious
proof; then how could the statement by positive concomitance when negative concomitance is given,

children.text: वैधर्म्यवचने वा साधर्म्यवचनं पराजयाय प्रभवेत् ? । कथं चैवं वादिप्रतिवादिनोः पक्षप्रति
children.translated_text: or the statement by positive concomitance when negative concomitance is given, serve as a ground for defeat? And how in this case would there not be futility of the adoption of thesis and counter-thesis by proponent and respondent,

children.text: पक्षपरिग्रहवैयर्थ्यं न स्यात्, क्वचिदेकत्रापि पक्षे साधनसामर्थ्यज्ञानाज्ञानयोः सम्भवात् ?
children.translated_text: since knowledge and ignorance of the power of proof can exist in the case of even a single thesis?

children.text: न खलु शब्दादौ नित्यत्वस्यानित्यत्वस्य वा परीक्षायामेकस्य साधनसामर्थ्ये ज्ञानमन्यस्य
children.translated_text: It is certainly not the case that in the examination of permanence or impermanence of sound etc., one person's knowledge of the power of proof and another's
ignorance is not the basis of victory and defeat

children.text: वा निबन्धनं न भवति । युगपत्साधनासामर्थ्यज्ञाने च
children.translated_text: respectively. And if both the proponent and respondent simultaneously know [or are ignorant of] the power of proof,

children.text: वादिप्रतिवादिनोः कस्य जयः पराजयो वा स्यादविशेषात् ? । न कस्यचिदिति चेत्; तर्हि
children.translated_text: whose victory or defeat would it be, there being no distinction? If none; then since the proponent who commits the fault of excess statement
is established to be ignorant of the power of proof, and since the respondent, by raising the fault of excess
statement, is established to know only that fault,

children.text: त्रज्ञानसिद्धेर्न कस्यचिज्जयः पराजयो वा स्यात् । नहि यो
children.translated_text: there would be neither victory nor defeat for anyone. For one who knows

children.text: यद्दोषं वेत्ति स तद्गुणमपि, कुतश्चिन्मारणशक्तौ वेदनेऽपि
children.translated_text: a particular fault of something does not necessarily know its virtue, just as even when the killing power of a poisonous substance is known,
there is no awareness of its power to cure leprosy.

children.text: शक्तौ संवेदनानुदयात् । तन्न तत्सामर्थ्यज्ञानाज्ञाननिबन्धनौ जयपराजयौ व्यवस्थाप
children.translated_text: Therefore, victory and defeat cannot be established as based on knowledge and ignorance of the power [of proof],

children.text: यितुं शक्यौ, यथोक्तदोषानुषङ्गात् । स्वपक्षसिद्ध्यसिद्धिनिबन्धनौ तु तौ निरवद्यौ पक्ष
children.translated_text: since the stated faults would follow. But when those [victory and defeat] are based on the establishment or non-establishment of one's own position, they are faultless, since there is no futility of adopting a thesis
and counter-thesis. When the establishment of one's own position by someone through some [means]
is firmly determined, the other's
lack of such establishment results in victory and defeat occurring at once.
If it be objected that victory and defeat are not based on the establishment or non-establishment of one's own position, but are based on knowledge and ignorance—

children.text: मात्रम्-अदोषोद्भावनम्, पर्युदासे तु दोषाभासानामन्यदोषाणां चोद्भावनं प्रतिवादिनो निग्रह
children.translated_text: i.e. non-pointing-out of faults; in the case of implicative negation (<s>paryudāsa</s>), pointing out pseudo-faults and other [irrelevant] faults is a <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat) for the respondent—

children.text: स्थानमिति--तत् वादिनाऽदोषवति साधने प्रयुक्ते सत्यनुमतमेव यदि वादी स्वपक्षं साध
children.translated_text: this is accepted only if the proponent has employed a faultless proof and if the proponent actually establishes his own position,

children.text: येन्नान्यथा । वचनाधिक्यं तु दोषः प्रागेव प्रतिविहितः । यथैव हि पञ्चावयवप्रयोगे
children.translated_text: not otherwise. The fault of excess statement has already been refuted above. For just as in the five-membered syllogism
excess statement

children.text: निग्रहस्थानं तथा त्र्यवयवप्रयोगे न्यूनतापि स्याद्विशेषाभावात् । प्रतिज्ञा
children.translated_text: is a <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat), so too in the three-membered syllogism, deficiency (<s>nyūnatā</s>) should also be [a point of defeat], there being no difference. For the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>)
and the other [members], all five, are components of inference (<s>anumāna</s>)—
Thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>), application (<s>upanaya</s>), and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) are the members [of a syllogism].
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.32
—as stated thus. When even one among them is not stated, the fault called deficiency (<s>nyūnatā</s>)
necessarily follows,
since 'that which lacks even one [member] is deficient'—
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.12
as stated.
Therefore, in determining victory and its opposite [defeat], there is no other cause apart from the cause already stated. Enough of this digression. [End of verse 35.]
And the interpretation of 'failure to point out faults'—in the case of absolute negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>), it is merely the absence of pointing out faults,

children.text: मत्रावश्याभिधातव्यं यतो नाविज्ञातस्वरूपस्यास्यावलम्बनं जयाय प्रभवति न चावि
children.translated_text: must necessarily be stated, since clinging to [a position] whose true nature is not understood does not lead to victory; nor can
one pierce a counter-leaf (<s>parapatra</s>) whose true nature is not understood — he says:

children.text: ॥ छ ॥ श्रीः ॥ छ ॥ मङ्गलम् ॥ महाश्रीः ॥ छ ॥ श्री ॥--
--॰ मित्याहुः । इत्याचार्यश्री ५ श्रीहेमचन्द्रविरचितायाः प्रमाणमीमांसायास्तद्वृत्तेश्च द्वितीयस्याध्यायस्य प्रथमाह्निकं
समाप्तम् ॥ श्री ॥ संवत् १७०७ वर्षे मार्गशीर्षमासे कृष्णतृतीयायां पुण्यतिथौ रविवासरे श्रीअणहिल्लपुरपत्तनमध्ये
पुस्तकं लिखितमिदं ॥ छ ॥ शुभं भवतु ॥ श्रीकल्याणमस्तु ॥ १ ॥ श्री ॥ १ ॥ छ ॥ छ ॥ १ ॥--

children.translated_text: And this previously described fourfold debate (<s>vāda</s>) sometimes also requires a written document (<s>patrālambana</s>); hence its definition—
